Sibawayh said: Qalun claimed that in some copies of the Qur'an it reads "wadda law tudhin fa-yudhinu" without the nun, and the accusative is according to the response to the wish (jawab al-tamanni) implied by "wadda." The apparent meaning of idhan in the language is what we mentioned first.

﴿And do not obey every frequent swearer﴾, that is, one who often swears falsely. ﴿Contemptible﴾ is on the pattern fa'il from mahanah, which means lack of judgement and discernment.

Mujahid said: it is the liar.

Qatadah said: one who excessively engages in evil; al-Hasan said the same.

It was said: he is the wicked and weak, and it was said: the one who is contemptible in the sight of Allah, and it was said: the abject, and it was said: the base.

﴿A defamer, going about with slander﴾. al-Hammaz is one who backbites people.

Ibn Zayd said: he is one who taunts his brother. It was also said: al-hammaz is one who mentions people to their faces, and al-lammaz is one who mentions them in their absence. So said Abu al-Aliyah, al-Hasan and Ata ibn Abi Rabah. Muqatil said the opposite.

Al-mashsha'  bi-namim is one who walks about with tale-bearing (namimah) among the people to cause corruption between them. It is said: "nammá yannimmu," when he carries corruption among people. From it is the words of the poet:

"A client like a nest of ants, having no good in him
For his master except his tale-bearing."

It was said: al-namim is the plural of namimah.

﴿Preventing good﴾, that is, stingy with wealth, not spending it in its proper place. It was said: he is one who prevents his family and clan from Islam.

al-Hasan said: he says to them, "Whoever among you enters the religion of Muhammad, I will never benefit him with anything."

﴿Transgressing, sinful﴾, that is, exceeding the limit in wrongdoing, abundant in sin.

﴿Ughull﴾. al-Wahidi said: the exegetes say he is one of harsh constitution and foul character.

al-Farra' said: he is one very contentious in falsehood.

al-Zajjaj said: he is the coarse and rough.

al-Layth said: he is the greedy and withholding. It is said: "I ataltu al-rajul u'tiluhu," when I pulled a man with violent force. From it is the words of the poet:

"We strike him with a blow, and we do not drag him."

﴿After that, a bastard﴾. That is, after all he has counted of his faults, he is a zanim. The zanim is the illegitimate claimant who is attached to a people though he is not one of them. It is derived from the zanamah, the dangling flap at the throat of a sheep or goat. From it is the words of Hassan:

"A bastard whom men claimed as an addition,
As the forelegs are added to the hide's width."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the zanim is one known for evil. It was said: he was from Quraysh and had a zanamah like the zanamah of a sheep. It was also said: he is the wrongdoer.

﴿Because he has wealth and sons﴾. This is connected to His words "do not obey," meaning: do not obey one whose faults are these, because he has wealth and sons.

al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: that is, "because he has," meaning: do not obey him for his wealth and his sons.

Ibn Amir, Abu Ja'far, al-Mughirah and Abu Haywah recited "an kana" with a single long hamzah, as an interrogative.

Hamzah, Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal recited "a-an kana" with two lightened hamzahs. The rest recited with a single hamzah as a statement. On the reading of the interrogative, the meaning is reproach and rebuke, since he repaid the blessings Allah had granted him of wealth and sons by disbelieving in Him and His Messenger.

Nafi', in one narration from him, recited it with a kasra on the hamzah, as a conditional.

﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Myths of the ancients."﴾ This is a new sentence functioning as an explanation of the prohibition. The meaning of "myths of the ancients" has been explained in several places earlier.

﴿We will brand him upon the snout﴾, that is, We will brand him with a mark on his snout.

Abu Ubaydah, Abu Zayd and al-Mubarrad said: al-khurtum is the nose.

Muqatil said: We will mark him with blackness on the nose, because his face will blacken before entering the Fire.

al-Farra' said: though the snout is specifically singled out for the mark, it is in the sense of the face, since part of the face stands for part of it.

al-Zajjaj said: a sign will be placed on him in the Hereafter by which the people of the Fire are recognized, through the blackening of their faces.

Qatadah said: We will attach to him something that never leaves him. Ibn Qutaybah chose this view and said: the Arabs say, "He has branded him with an evil brand," meaning that they attached to him a shame that never leaves him. So the meaning is that Allah attached to him a shame that never leaves him, like a mark on the snout. It was also said: the meaning of "We will brand him" is "We will strike him with the sword."

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: the meaning is "We will punish him for drinking wine," and wine is sometimes called al-kharTum (lit. "the snout"). From this is the saying of the poet:

"You spend your day in amusement and merriment, / and at night you are a drinker of the kharatim (wine-cups/wine)."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Saʿid ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-ʿAzama, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, narrated (it);

and Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat, al-Khatib in his Tarikh, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtara, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it, "Write!" It said, "O Lord, what shall I write?" He said, "Write the decree." So what is to be has flowed from that day until the Hour arises. Then the Record was folded up and the pen was lifted. His Throne was upon the water. The vapour of the water rose, and from it the heavens were split open. Then the Nun was created, and the earth was spread upon it, and the earth rests on the back of the Nun. The Nun moved, so the earth shook, and the mountains were set firm upon it, for the mountains boast over the earth until the Day of Resurrection. Then Ibn ʿAbbas recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿUbada ibn al-Samit, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it, 'Write!' So it wrote what is to be until eternity."

Ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of Muʿawiya ibn Qurra, from his father, with a marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet) report similar to it.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: God created the Nun, which is the inkwell, and created the pen, and said to it, "Write!" It said, "What shall I write?" He said, "Write what is to be until the Day of Resurrection."

al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi narrated from Abu Hurayra, marfuʿ, something similar.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Nun" is the inkwell.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The Nun is the fish upon which rests the earths, and the pen with which our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, wrote the decree, its good and its evil, its harm and its benefit." ﴿And what they inscribe﴾ — he said: "the noble scribes."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, narrated through several chains from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, that he said: "what they write."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, he said: "and what they know."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Muslim, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Saʿd ibn Hisham, who said: I came to ʿAisha and said, "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the character (khuluq) of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." She said: "His character was the Qur'an. Do you not read the Qur'an? ﴿Indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾."

Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nuʿaym in al-Dala'il, and al-Wahidi narrated from her, who said: "No one had better character than the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Whenever any of his companions or of his household called him, he would say, 'Labbayka' (here I am). For this reason God revealed: ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Abu al-Darda', who said: "ʿAisha was asked about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and she said: 'His character was the Qur'an: he was pleased with what pleases it, and angry at what angers it.'"

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Tirmidhi, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Jadali, who said: "I asked ʿAisha: 'What was the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)?' She said: 'He was not obscene nor given to obscenity, nor did he shout in the markets, nor did he repay evil with evil, but he pardoned and overlooked.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: ﴿So you will see and they will see﴾, he said: "You will know and they will know on the Day of Resurrection." ﴿Which of you is the afflicted (al-maftun)?﴾ He said: "The devil." They used to say, "He is a devil and he is a madman."

Ibn Jarir narrated from him concerning the verse: "Which of you is the madman (al-majnun)?"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him concerning His words: ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾, he said: "They wish you would grant them concessions, so they would grant you concessions."

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him concerning ﴿And do not obey every oath-swearing contemptible one﴾ up to the end of the verse, he said: "He means al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu ʿUthman al-Nahdi, who said: Marwan said, when the people pledged allegiance to Yazid: "It is the sunna of Abu Bakr and ʿUmar." ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said: "It is not the sunna of Abu Bakr and ʿUmar, but it is the sunna of Heraclius." Marwan said: "This is the one about whom was revealed: ﴿And he who said to his parents, 'Uff to you both!'﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 17], the verse..." ʿAisha heard that and said: "It was not revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Rahman, but it was revealed concerning your father: ﴿And do not obey every oath-swearing contemptible one, backbiting slanderer, going about with malicious talk﴾."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "There was revealed upon the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And do not obey every oath-swearing contemptible one, backbiting slanderer, going about with malicious talk﴾, and we did not know (who was meant) until there was revealed upon him: ﴿Besides all that, ignoble (zanim)﴾, and then we knew him: he had a mark like the wattle of a sheep."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: "The ʿutull is the illegitimately claimed (al-da'i), and the zanim is the suspicious one who is known for evil."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn ʿAsakir narrated from him: "The zanim is the da'i."

al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, narrated from him also: "The zanim is one known for evil, as a sheep is known by its wattle."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: "He is a man who passes by a people, and they say, 'A bad man.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him concerning His words ﴿zanim﴾: "He is oppressive (zalum)." It has also been said: these verses were revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, and it has been said: concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.

This surah is Makki according to al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata and Jabir.

It is reported from Ibn Abbas and Qatadah that from its beginning up to His words ﴿We will brand him upon the snout﴾ it is Makki (revealed in Makkah), and from after that up to His words ﴿among the righteous﴾ it is Madani (revealed in Madinah), and the rest of it is Makki. So said al-Mawardi.

Ibn al-Durays reported from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Whenever the opening of a surah was revealed in Makkah, it was written in Makkah, and then Allah added to it what He willed. The first of the Qur'an to be revealed was ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾, then ﴿Nun﴾, then al-Muzzammil, then al-Muddaththir."

al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi reported from him: "The surah of ﴿Nun﴾ was revealed in Makkah." Ibn Mardawayh reported the same from Aishah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His words ﴿Nun﴾: Abu Bakr, Warsh, Ibn Amir, al-Kisa'i, Ibn Muhaysin and Ibn Hubayrah recited it with idgham (assimilation, merging the second nun of its spelling into the waw), while the rest recited it with izhar (clear pronunciation). Abu Amr and Isa ibn Umar recited it with a fatha, on the basis of an implied verb.

Ibn Amir, Nasr and Ibn Ishaq recited it with a kasra, either on the basis of an implied oath or because of the meeting of two sakins (unvowelled letters). Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa' and Harun recited it with a damma, as an indeclinable form (bina').

Mujahid, Muqatil and al-Suddi said: it is the fish that carries the earth. Murrah al-Hamadhani, Ata al-Khurasani and al-Kalbi also said this.

It was also said that the nun is the last letter of the word al-Rahman.

Ibn Zayd said: it is an oath which Allah swore by.

Ibn Kaysan said: it is the opening of the surah.

Ata and Abu al-Aliyah said: it is the nun of nasr (help) and nasir (helper). Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Allah swore by His help to the believers.

It was also said: it is one of the letters of the alphabet, like the openings found at the beginnings of surahs that begin with such letters. We have already explained the correct view regarding such openings at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.

The waw in His words ﴿and the pen﴾ is the waw of oath: Allah swore by the pen because of what it contains of clarification (bayan). It applies to every pen with which something is written. A group of exegetes said: what is meant is the pen with which the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) was written, and Allah swore by it in glorification of it.

Qatadah said: the pen is among the blessings of Allah upon His servants.

﴿And what they inscribe﴾: "ma" here is a relative pronoun (mawsulah), meaning "and those who inscribe." The pronoun refers back to the people of the pen, who are indicated by its mention, since mention of the instrument of writing points to the writer.

The meaning is: "and those who inscribe," that is, who write everything that is written. Or it refers to the guardian angels (al-hafazah) mentioned earlier.

It is permissible for "ma" to be a verbal noun (masdariyyah), meaning "and their inscribing." It was also said that the pronoun refers to the pen alone, by way of attributing the verb to the instrument and treating it as though it were rational.

The answer to the oath is His words ﴿You are not, by the blessing of your Lord, a madman﴾. "Ma" is negating, "anta" is its subject, and "bi-majnun" is its predicate.

al-Zajjaj said: "anta" is the subject of "ma," "bi-majnun" is its predicate, and His words ﴿by the blessing of your Lord﴾ are a parenthetical statement placed in the middle. The meaning is: madness has been removed from you by the blessing of your Lord, just as one says "you are sane, by the praise of Allah."

It was said: the "ba" is attached to an implied word functioning as a circumstantial state (hal), as if it were said: "You are free of madness, connected to the blessing of Allah, which is prophethood and general leadership."

It was also said: the "ba" is for oath, meaning: "By you and the blessing of your Lord, you are not a madman."

It was said: the blessing here is mercy, and the verse is a refutation of the disbelievers, who said ﴿O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, you are truly mad﴾ [al-Hijr: 6].

﴿And indeed for you is a reward﴾, that is, a recompense for what you bore of the burdens of prophethood and suffered of various hardships, ﴿unfailing﴾, that is, uninterrupted. It is said: "I cut the rope" when one severs it (manantu al-habl idha qata'tuh).

Mujahid said: ﴿unfailing﴾ means "not counted." al-Hasan said: ﴿unfailing﴾ means "not spoiled by reminding of favours (al-mann)."

al-Dahhak said: a reward without work. It was also said: "not measured out." It was said: "not reckoned as a favour against you by the people."

﴿And indeed you are upon a magnificent character﴾. It was said: it is Islam and the religion. Al-Wahidi reported this from most scholars.

It was said: it is the Qur'an. This was reported from al-Hasan and al-Awfi.

Qatadah said: it is what he used to act upon of Allah's commands and refrain from of Allah's prohibitions.

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that you are upon the character which Allah commanded you to have in the Qur'an. It was said: it is his gentleness toward his community and his honouring of them. It was said: the meaning is that you have a noble nature.

al-Mawardi said: this is the apparent meaning. The reality of "khuluq" (character) in the language is what a person trains himself to with good manners.

It is established in the Sahih, on the authority of Aishah, that she was asked about the character of the Prophet (ﷺ), and she said: "His character was the Qur'an." This sentence and the previous one are coordinated with the answer to the oath.

﴿So you will see and they will see﴾, that is: you, O Muhammad, will see, and the disbelievers will see, when the truth becomes clear and the covering is removed. That is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿which of you is the afflicted one﴾. The "ba" is extra, for emphasis, meaning: "which of you is afflicted with madness." So said al-Akhfash, Abu Ubaydah and others. A similar usage is the words of the poet:

"We are the sons of Ja'dah, companions of al-Ali'j,
We strike with the sword and hope for relief."

It was also said: the "ba" is not extra, and "al-maftun" is a verbal noun in the pattern of maf'ul, like al-ma'qul and al-maysur. The estimated meaning is: "with which of you is the affliction (al-futun) or the trial." From it is the words of the poet al-Ra'i:

"Until, when they left nothing of his bones
Flesh, nor of his heart, any intellect (ma'qul)."

That is, reason (aql).

al-Farra' said: the "ba" is in the sense of "fi" (in), meaning: "In which of you is the afflicted one? Is it in the group you are in, or in the other group?" The reading of Ibn Abi Ablah, "fi ayyikum al-maftun," supports this.

It was also said: the sentence contains an omitted modifier, meaning: "by which of you the afflicted one was afflicted," so the modifier is omitted and the modified noun placed in its position. This was also reported from al-Akhfash.

It was said: al-maftun is the one tormented, from the saying of the Arabs "I fatantu al-dhahab bi-al-nar" when I heated gold with fire. From it is His words ﴿on the day they will be tormented over the Fire﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 13].

It was said: al-maftun is the devil, because he is afflicted in his religion, meaning: "which of you is the devil."

Qatadah said: this is a warning to them of the punishment of the Day of Badr. The meaning is: "You will see, and the people of Makkah will see, when punishment descends upon them at Badr, which of you is the afflicted one."

The clause ﴿Indeed your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way﴾ is an explanation (ta'lil) of the clause before it, for it includes a judgement upon them of madness, because they opposed what benefits them in the immediate and the afterlife, and chose what harms them in both. The meaning is: He is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, which leads to the happiness of both abodes. ﴿And He is most knowing of the guided﴾ to His way, which leads to that happiness, both in this world and the next. So He rewards each doer according to his deed: if good, then good; if evil, then evil.

﴿So do not obey the deniers﴾. He, glorified is He, forbade him from leaning toward the polytheists, who were the leaders of the disbelievers of Makkah, because they used to call him to the religion of his fathers. So Allah forbade him to obey them. Or it is an indirect address to someone other than him, not to obey the disbelievers. Or obedience here means mere outward courtesy by showing what contradicts what is in the heart.

Allah forbade him from that, as His words indicate: ﴿They wish that you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾. Indeed, idhan (compromise) is softness, leniency and tolerance.

al-Farra' said: the meaning is: "they wish you would soften, so they would soften toward you." al-Kalbi also said this.

al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: "They wish you would disbelieve, so they would persist in disbelief."

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "They wish you would lie, so they would lie."

Qatadah said: "They wish you would turn away from this matter, so they would turn away with you."

al-Hasan said: "They wish you would flatter them in your religion, so they would flatter you."

Mujahid said: "They wish you would incline toward them and abandon what you are upon of truth, so they would lean toward you."

Ibn Qutaybah said: they wanted him to worship their gods for a period, and they would worship Allah for a period.

His words ﴿so they would compromise﴾ are coordinated (atf) with "you would compromise" and fall within the scope of "law" (if/would). Or it is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "so they compromise."

Sibawayh said: Qalun claimed that in some copies of the Qur'an it reads "wadda law tudhin fa-yudhinu" without the nun, and the accusative is according to the response to the wish (jawab al-tamanni) implied by "wadda." The apparent meaning of idhan in the language is what we mentioned first.

﴿And do not obey every frequent swearer﴾, that is, one who often swears falsely. ﴿Contemptible﴾ is on the pattern fa'il from mahanah, which means lack of judgement and discernment.

Mujahid said: it is the liar.

Qatadah said: one who excessively engages in evil; al-Hasan said the same.

It was said: he is the wicked and weak, and it was said: the one who is contemptible in the sight of Allah, and it was said: the abject, and it was said: the base.

﴿A defamer, going about with slander﴾. al-Hammaz is one who backbites people.

Ibn Zayd said: he is one who taunts his brother. It was also said: al-hammaz is one who mentions people to their faces, and al-lammaz is one who mentions them in their absence. So said Abu al-Aliyah, al-Hasan and Ata ibn Abi Rabah. Muqatil said the opposite.

Al-mashsha'  bi-namim is one who walks about with tale-bearing (namimah) among the people to cause corruption between them. It is said: "nammá yannimmu," when he carries corruption among people. From it is the words of the poet:

"A client like a nest of ants, having no good in him
For his master except his tale-bearing."

It was said: al-namim is the plural of namimah.

﴿Preventing good﴾, that is, stingy with wealth, not spending it in its proper place. It was said: he is one who prevents his family and clan from Islam.

al-Hasan said: he says to them, "Whoever among you enters the religion of Muhammad, I will never benefit him with anything."

﴿Transgressing, sinful﴾, that is, exceeding the limit in wrongdoing, abundant in sin.

﴿Ughull﴾. al-Wahidi said: the exegetes say he is one of harsh constitution and foul character.

al-Farra' said: he is one very contentious in falsehood.

al-Zajjaj said: he is the coarse and rough.

al-Layth said: he is the greedy and withholding. It is said: "I ataltu al-rajul u'tiluhu," when I pulled a man with violent force. From it is the words of the poet:

"We strike him with a blow, and we do not drag him."

﴿After that, a bastard﴾. That is, after all he has counted of his faults, he is a zanim. The zanim is the illegitimate claimant who is attached to a people though he is not one of them. It is derived from the zanamah, the dangling flap at the throat of a sheep or goat. From it is the words of Hassan:

"A bastard whom men claimed as an addition,
As the forelegs are added to the hide's width."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the zanim is one known for evil. It was said: he was from Quraysh and had a zanamah like the zanamah of a sheep. It was also said: he is the wrongdoer.

﴿Because he has wealth and sons﴾. This is connected to His words "do not obey," meaning: do not obey one whose faults are these, because he has wealth and sons.

al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: that is, "because he has," meaning: do not obey him for his wealth and his sons.

Ibn Amir, Abu Ja'far, al-Mughirah and Abu Haywah recited "an kana" with a single long hamzah, as an interrogative.

Hamzah, Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal recited "a-an kana" with two lightened hamzahs. The rest recited with a single hamzah as a statement. On the reading of the interrogative, the meaning is reproach and rebuke, since he repaid the blessings Allah had granted him of wealth and sons by disbelieving in Him and His Messenger.

Nafi', in one narration from him, recited it with a kasra on the hamzah, as a conditional.

﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Myths of the ancients."﴾ This is a new sentence functioning as an explanation of the prohibition. The meaning of "myths of the ancients" has been explained in several places earlier.

﴿We will brand him upon the snout﴾, that is, We will brand him with a mark on his snout.

Abu Ubaydah, Abu Zayd and al-Mubarrad said: al-khurtum is the nose.

Muqatil said: We will mark him with blackness on the nose, because his face will blacken before entering the Fire.

al-Farra' said: though the snout is specifically singled out for the mark, it is in the sense of the face, since part of the face stands for part of it.

al-Zajjaj said: a sign will be placed on him in the Hereafter by which the people of the Fire are recognized, through the blackening of their faces.

Qatadah said: We will attach to him something that never leaves him. Ibn Qutaybah chose this view and said: the Arabs say, "He has branded him with an evil brand," meaning that they attached to him a shame that never leaves him. So the meaning is that Allah attached to him a shame that never leaves him, like a mark on the snout. It was also said: the meaning of "We will brand him" is "We will strike him with the sword."

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: the meaning is "We will punish him for drinking wine," and wine is sometimes called al-kharTum (lit. "the snout"). From this is the saying of the poet:

"You spend your day in amusement and merriment, / and at night you are a drinker of the kharatim (wine-cups/wine)."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Saʿid ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-ʿAzama, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, narrated (it);

and Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat, al-Khatib in his Tarikh, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtara, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it, "Write!" It said, "O Lord, what shall I write?" He said, "Write the decree." So what is to be has flowed from that day until the Hour arises. Then the Record was folded up and the pen was lifted. His Throne was upon the water. The vapour of the water rose, and from it the heavens were split open. Then the Nun was created, and the earth was spread upon it, and the earth rests on the back of the Nun. The Nun moved, so the earth shook, and the mountains were set firm upon it, for the mountains boast over the earth until the Day of Resurrection. Then Ibn ʿAbbas recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿUbada ibn al-Samit, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it, 'Write!' So it wrote what is to be until eternity."

Ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of Muʿawiya ibn Qurra, from his father, with a marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet) report similar to it.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: God created the Nun, which is the inkwell, and created the pen, and said to it, "Write!" It said, "What shall I write?" He said, "Write what is to be until the Day of Resurrection."

al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi narrated from Abu Hurayra, marfuʿ, something similar.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Nun" is the inkwell.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The Nun is the fish upon which rests the earths, and the pen with which our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, wrote the decree, its good and its evil, its harm and its benefit." ﴿And what they inscribe﴾ — he said: "the noble scribes."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, narrated through several chains from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, that he said: "what they write."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, he said: "and what they know."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Muslim, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Saʿd ibn Hisham, who said: I came to ʿAisha and said, "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the character (khuluq) of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." She said: "His character was the Qur'an. Do you not read the Qur'an? ﴿Indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾."

Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nuʿaym in al-Dala'il, and al-Wahidi narrated from her, who said: "No one had better character than the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Whenever any of his companions or of his household called him, he would say, 'Labbayka' (here I am). For this reason God revealed: ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Abu al-Darda', who said: "ʿAisha was asked about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and she said: 'His character was the Qur'an: he was pleased with what pleases it, and angry at what angers it.'"

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Tirmidhi, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Jadali, who said: "I asked ʿAisha: 'What was the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)?' She said: 'He was not obscene nor given to obscenity, nor did he shout in the markets, nor did he repay evil with evil, but he pardoned and overlooked.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: ﴿So you will see and they will see﴾, he said: "You will know and they will know on the Day of Resurrection." ﴿Which of you is the afflicted (al-maftun)?﴾ He said: "The devil." They used to say, "He is a devil and he is a madman."

Ibn Jarir narrated from him concerning the verse: "Which of you is the madman (al-majnun)?"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him concerning His words: ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾, he said: "They wish you would grant them concessions, so they would grant you concessions."

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him concerning ﴿And do not obey every oath-swearing contemptible one﴾ up to the end of the verse, he said: "He means al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu ʿUthman al-Nahdi, who said: Marwan said, when the people pledged allegiance to Yazid: "It is the sunna of Abu Bakr and ʿUmar." ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said: "It is not the sunna of Abu Bakr and ʿUmar, but it is the sunna of Heraclius." Marwan said: "This is the one about whom was revealed: ﴿And he who said to his parents, 'Uff to you both!'﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 17], the verse..." ʿAisha heard that and said: "It was not revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Rahman, but it was revealed concerning your father: ﴿And do not obey every oath-swearing contemptible one, backbiting slanderer, going about with malicious talk﴾."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "There was revealed upon the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And do not obey every oath-swearing contemptible one, backbiting slanderer, going about with malicious talk﴾, and we did not know (who was meant) until there was revealed upon him: ﴿Besides all that, ignoble (zanim)﴾, and then we knew him: he had a mark like the wattle of a sheep."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: "The ʿutull is the illegitimately claimed (al-da'i), and the zanim is the suspicious one who is known for evil."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn ʿAsakir narrated from him: "The zanim is the da'i."

al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, narrated from him also: "The zanim is one known for evil, as a sheep is known by its wattle."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: "He is a man who passes by a people, and they say, 'A bad man.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him concerning His words ﴿zanim﴾: "He is oppressive (zalum)." It has also been said: these verses were revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, and it has been said: concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.

This surah is Makki according to al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata and Jabir.

It is reported from Ibn Abbas and Qatadah that from its beginning up to His words ﴿We will brand him upon the snout﴾ it is Makki (revealed in Makkah), and from after that up to His words ﴿among the righteous﴾ it is Madani (revealed in Madinah), and the rest of it is Makki. So said al-Mawardi.

Ibn al-Durays reported from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Whenever the opening of a surah was revealed in Makkah, it was written in Makkah, and then Allah added to it what He willed. The first of the Qur'an to be revealed was ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾, then ﴿Nun﴾, then al-Muzzammil, then al-Muddaththir."

al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi reported from him: "The surah of ﴿Nun﴾ was revealed in Makkah." Ibn Mardawayh reported the same from Aishah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His words ﴿Nun﴾: Abu Bakr, Warsh, Ibn Amir, al-Kisa'i, Ibn Muhaysin and Ibn Hubayrah recited it with idgham (assimilation, merging the second nun of its spelling into the waw), while the rest recited it with izhar (clear pronunciation). Abu Amr and Isa ibn Umar recited it with a fatha, on the basis of an implied verb.

Ibn Amir, Nasr and Ibn Ishaq recited it with a kasra, either on the basis of an implied oath or because of the meeting of two sakins (unvowelled letters). Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa' and Harun recited it with a damma, as an indeclinable form (bina').

Mujahid, Muqatil and al-Suddi said: it is the fish that carries the earth. Murrah al-Hamadhani, Ata al-Khurasani and al-Kalbi also said this.

It was also said that the nun is the last letter of the word al-Rahman.

Ibn Zayd said: it is an oath which Allah swore by.

Ibn Kaysan said: it is the opening of the surah.

Ata and Abu al-Aliyah said: it is the nun of nasr (help) and nasir (helper). Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Allah swore by His help to the believers.

It was also said: it is one of the letters of the alphabet, like the openings found at the beginnings of surahs that begin with such letters. We have already explained the correct view regarding such openings at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.

The waw in His words ﴿and the pen﴾ is the waw of oath: Allah swore by the pen because of what it contains of clarification (bayan). It applies to every pen with which something is written. A group of exegetes said: what is meant is the pen with which the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) was written, and Allah swore by it in glorification of it.

Qatadah said: the pen is among the blessings of Allah upon His servants.

﴿And what they inscribe﴾: "ma" here is a relative pronoun (mawsulah), meaning "and those who inscribe." The pronoun refers back to the people of the pen, who are indicated by its mention, since mention of the instrument of writing points to the writer.

The meaning is: "and those who inscribe," that is, who write everything that is written. Or it refers to the guardian angels (al-hafazah) mentioned earlier.

It is permissible for "ma" to be a verbal noun (masdariyyah), meaning "and their inscribing." It was also said that the pronoun refers to the pen alone, by way of attributing the verb to the instrument and treating it as though it were rational.

The answer to the oath is His words ﴿You are not, by the blessing of your Lord, a madman﴾. "Ma" is negating, "anta" is its subject, and "bi-majnun" is its predicate.

al-Zajjaj said: "anta" is the subject of "ma," "bi-majnun" is its predicate, and His words ﴿by the blessing of your Lord﴾ are a parenthetical statement placed in the middle. The meaning is: madness has been removed from you by the blessing of your Lord, just as one says "you are sane, by the praise of Allah."

It was said: the "ba" is attached to an implied word functioning as a circumstantial state (hal), as if it were said: "You are free of madness, connected to the blessing of Allah, which is prophethood and general leadership."

It was also said: the "ba" is for oath, meaning: "By you and the blessing of your Lord, you are not a madman."

It was said: the blessing here is mercy, and the verse is a refutation of the disbelievers, who said ﴿O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, you are truly mad﴾ [al-Hijr: 6].

﴿And indeed for you is a reward﴾, that is, a recompense for what you bore of the burdens of prophethood and suffered of various hardships, ﴿unfailing﴾, that is, uninterrupted. It is said: "I cut the rope" when one severs it (manantu al-habl idha qata'tuh).

Mujahid said: ﴿unfailing﴾ means "not counted." al-Hasan said: ﴿unfailing﴾ means "not spoiled by reminding of favours (al-mann)."

al-Dahhak said: a reward without work. It was also said: "not measured out." It was said: "not reckoned as a favour against you by the people."

﴿And indeed you are upon a magnificent character﴾. It was said: it is Islam and the religion. Al-Wahidi reported this from most scholars.

It was said: it is the Qur'an. This was reported from al-Hasan and al-Awfi.

Qatadah said: it is what he used to act upon of Allah's commands and refrain from of Allah's prohibitions.

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that you are upon the character which Allah commanded you to have in the Qur'an. It was said: it is his gentleness toward his community and his honouring of them. It was said: the meaning is that you have a noble nature.

al-Mawardi said: this is the apparent meaning. The reality of "khuluq" (character) in the language is what a person trains himself to with good manners.

It is established in the Sahih, on the authority of Aishah, that she was asked about the character of the Prophet (ﷺ), and she said: "His character was the Qur'an." This sentence and the previous one are coordinated with the answer to the oath.

﴿So you will see and they will see﴾, that is: you, O Muhammad, will see, and the disbelievers will see, when the truth becomes clear and the covering is removed. That is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿which of you is the afflicted one﴾. The "ba" is extra, for emphasis, meaning: "which of you is afflicted with madness." So said al-Akhfash, Abu Ubaydah and others. A similar usage is the words of the poet:

"We are the sons of Ja'dah, companions of al-Ali'j,
We strike with the sword and hope for relief."

It was also said: the "ba" is not extra, and "al-maftun" is a verbal noun in the pattern of maf'ul, like al-ma'qul and al-maysur. The estimated meaning is: "with which of you is the affliction (al-futun) or the trial." From it is the words of the poet al-Ra'i:

"Until, when they left nothing of his bones
Flesh, nor of his heart, any intellect (ma'qul)."

That is, reason (aql).

al-Farra' said: the "ba" is in the sense of "fi" (in), meaning: "In which of you is the afflicted one? Is it in the group you are in, or in the other group?" The reading of Ibn Abi Ablah, "fi ayyikum al-maftun," supports this.

It was also said: the sentence contains an omitted modifier, meaning: "by which of you the afflicted one was afflicted," so the modifier is omitted and the modified noun placed in its position. This was also reported from al-Akhfash.

It was said: al-maftun is the one tormented, from the saying of the Arabs "I fatantu al-dhahab bi-al-nar" when I heated gold with fire. From it is His words ﴿on the day they will be tormented over the Fire﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 13].

It was said: al-maftun is the devil, because he is afflicted in his religion, meaning: "which of you is the devil."

Qatadah said: this is a warning to them of the punishment of the Day of Badr. The meaning is: "You will see, and the people of Makkah will see, when punishment descends upon them at Badr, which of you is the afflicted one."

The clause ﴿Indeed your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way﴾ is an explanation (ta'lil) of the clause before it, for it includes a judgement upon them of madness, because they opposed what benefits them in the immediate and the afterlife, and chose what harms them in both. The meaning is: He is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, which leads to the happiness of both abodes. ﴿And He is most knowing of the guided﴾ to His way, which leads to that happiness, both in this world and the next. So He rewards each doer according to his deed: if good, then good; if evil, then evil.

﴿So do not obey the deniers﴾. He, glorified is He, forbade him from leaning toward the polytheists, who were the leaders of the disbelievers of Makkah, because they used to call him to the religion of his fathers. So Allah forbade him to obey them. Or it is an indirect address to someone other than him, not to obey the disbelievers. Or obedience here means mere outward courtesy by showing what contradicts what is in the heart.

Allah forbade him from that, as His words indicate: ﴿They wish that you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾. Indeed, idhan (compromise) is softness, leniency and tolerance.

al-Farra' said: the meaning is: "they wish you would soften, so they would soften toward you." al-Kalbi also said this.

al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: "They wish you would disbelieve, so they would persist in disbelief."

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "They wish you would lie, so they would lie."

Qatadah said: "They wish you would turn away from this matter, so they would turn away with you."

al-Hasan said: "They wish you would flatter them in your religion, so they would flatter you."

Mujahid said: "They wish you would incline toward them and abandon what you are upon of truth, so they would lean toward you."

Ibn Qutaybah said: they wanted him to worship their gods for a period, and they would worship Allah for a period.

His words ﴿so they would compromise﴾ are coordinated (atf) with "you would compromise" and fall within the scope of "law" (if/would). Or it is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "so they compromise."

Sibawayh said: Qalun claimed that in some copies of the Qur'an it reads "wadda law tudhin fa-yudhinu" without the nun, and the accusative is according to the response to the wish (jawab al-tamanni) implied by "wadda." The apparent meaning of idhan in the language is what we mentioned first.

﴿And do not obey every frequent swearer﴾, that is, one who often swears falsely. ﴿Contemptible﴾ is on the pattern fa'il from mahanah, which means lack of judgement and discernment.

Mujahid said: it is the liar.

Qatadah said: one who excessively engages in evil; al-Hasan said the same.

It was said: he is the wicked and weak, and it was said: the one who is contemptible in the sight of Allah, and it was said: the abject, and it was said: the base.

﴿A defamer, going about with slander﴾. al-Hammaz is one who backbites people.

Ibn Zayd said: he is one who taunts his brother. It was also said: al-hammaz is one who mentions people to their faces, and al-lammaz is one who mentions them in their absence. So said Abu al-Aliyah, al-Hasan and Ata ibn Abi Rabah. Muqatil said the opposite.

Al-mashsha'  bi-namim is one who walks about with tale-bearing (namimah) among the people to cause corruption between them. It is said: "nammá yannimmu," when he carries corruption among people. From it is the words of the poet:

"A client like a nest of ants, having no good in him
For his master except his tale-bearing."

It was said: al-namim is the plural of namimah.

﴿Preventing good﴾, that is, stingy with wealth, not spending it in its proper place. It was said: he is one who prevents his family and clan from Islam.

al-Hasan said: he says to them, "Whoever among you enters the religion of Muhammad, I will never benefit him with anything."

﴿Transgressing, sinful﴾, that is, exceeding the limit in wrongdoing, abundant in sin.

﴿Ughull﴾. al-Wahidi said: the exegetes say he is one of harsh constitution and foul character.

al-Farra' said: he is one very contentious in falsehood.

al-Zajjaj said: he is the coarse and rough.

al-Layth said: he is the greedy and withholding. It is said: "I ataltu al-rajul u'tiluhu," when I pulled a man with violent force. From it is the words of the poet:

"We strike him with a blow, and we do not drag him."

﴿After that, a bastard﴾. That is, after all he has counted of his faults, he is a zanim. The zanim is the illegitimate claimant who is attached to a people though he is not one of them. It is derived from the zanamah, the dangling flap at the throat of a sheep or goat. From it is the words of Hassan:

"A bastard whom men claimed as an addition,
As the forelegs are added to the hide's width."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the zanim is one known for evil. It was said: he was from Quraysh and had a zanamah like the zanamah of a sheep. It was also said: he is the wrongdoer.

﴿Because he has wealth and sons﴾. This is connected to His words "do not obey," meaning: do not obey one whose faults are these, because he has wealth and sons.

al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: that is, "because he has," meaning: do not obey him for his wealth and his sons.

Ibn Amir, Abu Ja'far, al-Mughirah and Abu Haywah recited "an kana" with a single long hamzah, as an interrogative.

Hamzah, Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal recited "a-an kana" with two lightened hamzahs. The rest recited with a single hamzah as a statement. On the reading of the interrogative, the meaning is reproach and rebuke, since he repaid the blessings Allah had granted him of wealth and sons by disbelieving in Him and His Messenger.

Nafi', in one narration from him, recited it with a kasra on the hamzah, as a conditional.

﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Myths of the ancients."﴾ This is a new sentence functioning as an explanation of the prohibition. The meaning of "myths of the ancients" has been explained in several places earlier.

﴿We will brand him upon the snout﴾, that is, We will brand him with a mark on his snout.

Abu Ubaydah, Abu Zayd and al-Mubarrad said: al-khurtum is the nose.

Muqatil said: We will mark him with blackness on the nose, because his face will blacken before entering the Fire.

al-Farra' said: though the snout is specifically singled out for the mark, it is in the sense of the face, since part of the face stands for part of it.

al-Zajjaj said: a sign will be placed on him in the Hereafter by which the people of the Fire are recognized, through the blackening of their faces.

Qatadah said: We will attach to him something that never leaves him. Ibn Qutaybah chose this view and said: the Arabs say, "He has branded him with an evil brand," meaning that they attached to him a shame that never leaves him. So the meaning is that Allah attached to him a shame that never leaves him, like a mark on the snout. It was also said: the meaning of "We will brand him" is "We will strike him with the sword."

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: the meaning is "We will punish him for drinking wine," and wine is sometimes called al-kharTum (lit. "the snout"). From this is the saying of the poet:

"You spend your day in amusement and merriment, / and at night you are a drinker of the kharatim (wine-cups/wine)."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Saʿid ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-ʿAzama, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, narrated (it);

and Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat, al-Khatib in his Tarikh, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtara, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it, "Write!" It said, "O Lord, what shall I write?" He said, "Write the decree." So what is to be has flowed from that day until the Hour arises. Then the Record was folded up and the pen was lifted. His Throne was upon the water. The vapour of the water rose, and from it the heavens were split open. Then the Nun was created, and the earth was spread upon it, and the earth rests on the back of the Nun. The Nun moved, so the earth shook, and the mountains were set firm upon it, for the mountains boast over the earth until the Day of Resurrection. Then Ibn ʿAbbas recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿUbada ibn al-Samit, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it, 'Write!' So it wrote what is to be until eternity."

Ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of Muʿawiya ibn Qurra, from his father, with a marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet) report similar to it.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: God created the Nun, which is the inkwell, and created the pen, and said to it, "Write!" It said, "What shall I write?" He said, "Write what is to be until the Day of Resurrection."

al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi narrated from Abu Hurayra, marfuʿ, something similar.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Nun" is the inkwell.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The Nun is the fish upon which rests the earths, and the pen with which our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, wrote the decree, its good and its evil, its harm and its benefit." ﴿And what they inscribe﴾ — he said: "the noble scribes."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, narrated through several chains from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, that he said: "what they write."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, he said: "and what they know."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Muslim, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Saʿd ibn Hisham, who said: I came to ʿAisha and said, "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the character (khuluq) of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." She said: "His character was the Qur'an. Do you not read the Qur'an? ﴿Indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾."

Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nuʿaym in al-Dala'il, and al-Wahidi narrated from her, who said: "No one had better character than the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Whenever any of his companions or of his household called him, he would say, 'Labbayka' (here I am). For this reason God revealed: ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Abu al-Darda', who said: "ʿAisha was asked about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and she said: 'His character was the Qur'an: he was pleased with what pleases it, and angry at what angers it.'"

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Tirmidhi, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Jadali, who said: "I asked ʿAisha: 'What was the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)?' She said: 'He was not obscene nor given to obscenity, nor did he shout in the markets, nor did he repay evil with evil, but he pardoned and overlooked.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: ﴿So you will see and they will see﴾, he said: "You will know and they will know on the Day of Resurrection." ﴿Which of you is the afflicted (al-maftun)?﴾ He said: "The devil." They used to say, "He is a devil and he is a madman."

Ibn Jarir narrated from him concerning the verse: "Which of you is the madman (al-majnun)?"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him concerning His words: ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾, he said: "They wish you would grant them concessions, so they would grant you concessions."

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him concerning ﴿And do not obey every oath-swearing contemptible one﴾ up to the end of the verse, he said: "He means al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu ʿUthman al-Nahdi, who said: Marwan said, when the people pledged allegiance to Yazid: "It is the sunna of Abu Bakr and ʿUmar." ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said: "It is not the sunna of Abu Bakr and ʿUmar, but it is the sunna of Heraclius." Marwan said: "This is the one about whom was revealed: ﴿And he who said to his parents, 'Uff to you both!'﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 17], the verse..." ʿAisha heard that and said: "It was not revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Rahman, but it was revealed concerning your father: ﴿And do not obey every oath-swearing contemptible one, backbiting slanderer, going about with malicious talk﴾."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "There was revealed upon the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And do not obey every oath-swearing contemptible one, backbiting slanderer, going about with malicious talk﴾, and we did not know (who was meant) until there was revealed upon him: ﴿Besides all that, ignoble (zanim)﴾, and then we knew him: he had a mark like the wattle of a sheep."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: "The ʿutull is the illegitimately claimed (al-da'i), and the zanim is the suspicious one who is known for evil."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn ʿAsakir narrated from him: "The zanim is the da'i."

al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, narrated from him also: "The zanim is one known for evil, as a sheep is known by its wattle."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: "He is a man who passes by a people, and they say, 'A bad man.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him concerning His words ﴿zanim﴾: "He is oppressive (zalum)." It has also been said: these verses were revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, and it has been said: concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.

This surah is Makki according to al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata and Jabir.

It is reported from Ibn Abbas and Qatadah that from its beginning up to His words ﴿We will brand him upon the snout﴾ it is Makki (revealed in Makkah), and from after that up to His words ﴿among the righteous﴾ it is Madani (revealed in Madinah), and the rest of it is Makki. So said al-Mawardi.

Ibn al-Durays reported from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Whenever the opening of a surah was revealed in Makkah, it was written in Makkah, and then Allah added to it what He willed. The first of the Qur'an to be revealed was ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾, then ﴿Nun﴾, then al-Muzzammil, then al-Muddaththir."

al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi reported from him: "The surah of ﴿Nun﴾ was revealed in Makkah." Ibn Mardawayh reported the same from Aishah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His words ﴿Nun﴾: Abu Bakr, Warsh, Ibn Amir, al-Kisa'i, Ibn Muhaysin and Ibn Hubayrah recited it with idgham (assimilation, merging the second nun of its spelling into the waw), while the rest recited it with izhar (clear pronunciation). Abu Amr and Isa ibn Umar recited it with a fatha, on the basis of an implied verb.

Ibn Amir, Nasr and Ibn Ishaq recited it with a kasra, either on the basis of an implied oath or because of the meeting of two sakins (unvowelled letters). Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa' and Harun recited it with a damma, as an indeclinable form (bina').

Mujahid, Muqatil and al-Suddi said: it is the fish that carries the earth. Murrah al-Hamadhani, Ata al-Khurasani and al-Kalbi also said this.

It was also said that the nun is the last letter of the word al-Rahman.

Ibn Zayd said: it is an oath which Allah swore by.

Ibn Kaysan said: it is the opening of the surah.

Ata and Abu al-Aliyah said: it is the nun of nasr (help) and nasir (helper). Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Allah swore by His help to the believers.

It was also said: it is one of the letters of the alphabet, like the openings found at the beginnings of surahs that begin with such letters. We have already explained the correct view regarding such openings at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.

The waw in His words ﴿and the pen﴾ is the waw of oath: Allah swore by the pen because of what it contains of clarification (bayan). It applies to every pen with which something is written. A group of exegetes said: what is meant is the pen with which the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) was written, and Allah swore by it in glorification of it.

Qatadah said: the pen is among the blessings of Allah upon His servants.

﴿And what they inscribe﴾: "ma" here is a relative pronoun (mawsulah), meaning "and those who inscribe." The pronoun refers back to the people of the pen, who are indicated by its mention, since mention of the instrument of writing points to the writer.

The meaning is: "and those who inscribe," that is, who write everything that is written. Or it refers to the guardian angels (al-hafazah) mentioned earlier.

It is permissible for "ma" to be a verbal noun (masdariyyah), meaning "and their inscribing." It was also said that the pronoun refers to the pen alone, by way of attributing the verb to the instrument and treating it as though it were rational.

The answer to the oath is His words ﴿You are not, by the blessing of your Lord, a madman﴾. "Ma" is negating, "anta" is its subject, and "bi-majnun" is its predicate.

al-Zajjaj said: "anta" is the subject of "ma," "bi-majnun" is its predicate, and His words ﴿by the blessing of your Lord﴾ are a parenthetical statement placed in the middle. The meaning is: madness has been removed from you by the blessing of your Lord, just as one says "you are sane, by the praise of Allah."

It was said: the "ba" is attached to an implied word functioning as a circumstantial state (hal), as if it were said: "You are free of madness, connected to the blessing of Allah, which is prophethood and general leadership."

It was also said: the "ba" is for oath, meaning: "By you and the blessing of your Lord, you are not a madman."

It was said: the blessing here is mercy, and the verse is a refutation of the disbelievers, who said ﴿O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, you are truly mad﴾ [al-Hijr: 6].

﴿And indeed for you is a reward﴾, that is, a recompense for what you bore of the burdens of prophethood and suffered of various hardships, ﴿unfailing﴾, that is, uninterrupted. It is said: "I cut the rope" when one severs it (manantu al-habl idha qata'tuh).

Mujahid said: ﴿unfailing﴾ means "not counted." al-Hasan said: ﴿unfailing﴾ means "not spoiled by reminding of favours (al-mann)."

al-Dahhak said: a reward without work. It was also said: "not measured out." It was said: "not reckoned as a favour against you by the people."

﴿And indeed you are upon a magnificent character﴾. It was said: it is Islam and the religion. Al-Wahidi reported this from most scholars.

It was said: it is the Qur'an. This was reported from al-Hasan and al-Awfi.

Qatadah said: it is what he used to act upon of Allah's commands and refrain from of Allah's prohibitions.

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that you are upon the character which Allah commanded you to have in the Qur'an. It was said: it is his gentleness toward his community and his honouring of them. It was said: the meaning is that you have a noble nature.

al-Mawardi said: this is the apparent meaning. The reality of "khuluq" (character) in the language is what a person trains himself to with good manners.

It is established in the Sahih, on the authority of Aishah, that she was asked about the character of the Prophet (ﷺ), and she said: "His character was the Qur'an." This sentence and the previous one are coordinated with the answer to the oath.

﴿So you will see and they will see﴾, that is: you, O Muhammad, will see, and the disbelievers will see, when the truth becomes clear and the covering is removed. That is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿which of you is the afflicted one﴾. The "ba" is extra, for emphasis, meaning: "which of you is afflicted with madness." So said al-Akhfash, Abu Ubaydah and others. A similar usage is the words of the poet:

"We are the sons of Ja'dah, companions of al-Ali'j,
We strike with the sword and hope for relief."

It was also said: the "ba" is not extra, and "al-maftun" is a verbal noun in the pattern of maf'ul, like al-ma'qul and al-maysur. The estimated meaning is: "with which of you is the affliction (al-futun) or the trial." From it is the words of the poet al-Ra'i:

"Until, when they left nothing of his bones
Flesh, nor of his heart, any intellect (ma'qul)."

That is, reason (aql).

al-Farra' said: the "ba" is in the sense of "fi" (in), meaning: "In which of you is the afflicted one? Is it in the group you are in, or in the other group?" The reading of Ibn Abi Ablah, "fi ayyikum al-maftun," supports this.

It was also said: the sentence contains an omitted modifier, meaning: "by which of you the afflicted one was afflicted," so the modifier is omitted and the modified noun placed in its position. This was also reported from al-Akhfash.

It was said: al-maftun is the one tormented, from the saying of the Arabs "I fatantu al-dhahab bi-al-nar" when I heated gold with fire. From it is His words ﴿on the day they will be tormented over the Fire﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 13].

It was said: al-maftun is the devil, because he is afflicted in his religion, meaning: "which of you is the devil."

Qatadah said: this is a warning to them of the punishment of the Day of Badr. The meaning is: "You will see, and the people of Makkah will see, when punishment descends upon them at Badr, which of you is the afflicted one."

The clause ﴿Indeed your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way﴾ is an explanation (ta'lil) of the clause before it, for it includes a judgement upon them of madness, because they opposed what benefits them in the immediate and the afterlife, and chose what harms them in both. The meaning is: He is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, which leads to the happiness of both abodes. ﴿And He is most knowing of the guided﴾ to His way, which leads to that happiness, both in this world and the next. So He rewards each doer according to his deed: if good, then good; if evil, then evil.

﴿So do not obey the deniers﴾. He, glorified is He, forbade him from leaning toward the polytheists, who were the leaders of the disbelievers of Makkah, because they used to call him to the religion of his fathers. So Allah forbade him to obey them. Or it is an indirect address to someone other than him, not to obey the disbelievers. Or obedience here means mere outward courtesy by showing what contradicts what is in the heart.

Allah forbade him from that, as His words indicate: ﴿They wish that you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾. Indeed, idhan (compromise) is softness, leniency and tolerance.

al-Farra' said: the meaning is: "they wish you would soften, so they would soften toward you." al-Kalbi also said this.

al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: "They wish you would disbelieve, so they would persist in disbelief."

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "They wish you would lie, so they would lie."

Qatadah said: "They wish you would turn away from this matter, so they would turn away with you."

al-Hasan said: "They wish you would flatter them in your religion, so they would flatter you."

Mujahid said: "They wish you would incline toward them and abandon what you are upon of truth, so they would lean toward you."

Ibn Qutaybah said: they wanted him to worship their gods for a period, and they would worship Allah for a period.

His words ﴿so they would compromise﴾ are coordinated (atf) with "you would compromise" and fall within the scope of "law" (if/would). Or it is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "so they compromise."

Sibawayh said: Qalun claimed that in some copies of the Qur'an it reads "wadda law tudhin fa-yudhinu" without the nun, and the accusative is according to the response to the wish (jawab al-tamanni) implied by "wadda." The apparent meaning of idhan in the language is what we mentioned first.

﴿And do not obey every frequent swearer﴾, that is, one who often swears falsely. ﴿Contemptible﴾ is on the pattern fa'il from mahanah, which means lack of judgement and discernment.

Mujahid said: it is the liar.

Qatadah said: one who excessively engages in evil; al-Hasan said the same.

It was said: he is the wicked and weak, and it was said: the one who is contemptible in the sight of Allah, and it was said: the abject, and it was said: the base.

﴿A defamer, going about with slander﴾. al-Hammaz is one who backbites people.

Ibn Zayd said: he is one who taunts his brother. It was also said: al-hammaz is one who mentions people to their faces, and al-lammaz is one who mentions them in their absence. So said Abu al-Aliyah, al-Hasan and Ata ibn Abi Rabah. Muqatil said the opposite.

Al-mashsha'  bi-namim is one who walks about with tale-bearing (namimah) among the people to cause corruption between them. It is said: "nammá yannimmu," when he carries corruption among people. From it is the words of the poet:

"A client like a nest of ants, having no good in him
For his master except his tale-bearing."

It was said: al-namim is the plural of namimah.

﴿Preventing good﴾, that is, stingy with wealth, not spending it in its proper place. It was said: he is one who prevents his family and clan from Islam.

al-Hasan said: he says to them, "Whoever among you enters the religion of Muhammad, I will never benefit him with anything."

﴿Transgressing, sinful﴾, that is, exceeding the limit in wrongdoing, abundant in sin.

﴿Ughull﴾. al-Wahidi said: the exegetes say he is one of harsh constitution and foul character.

al-Farra' said: he is one very contentious in falsehood.

al-Zajjaj said: he is the coarse and rough.

al-Layth said: he is the greedy and withholding. It is said: "I ataltu al-rajul u'tiluhu," when I pulled a man with violent force. From it is the words of the poet:

"We strike him with a blow, and we do not drag him."

﴿After that, a bastard﴾. That is, after all he has counted of his faults, he is a zanim. The zanim is the illegitimate claimant who is attached to a people though he is not one of them. It is derived from the zanamah, the dangling flap at the throat of a sheep or goat. From it is the words of Hassan:

"A bastard whom men claimed as an addition,
As the forelegs are added to the hide's width."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the zanim is one known for evil. It was said: he was from Quraysh and had a zanamah like the zanamah of a sheep. It was also said: he is the wrongdoer.

﴿Because he has wealth and sons﴾. This is connected to His words "do not obey," meaning: do not obey one whose faults are these, because he has wealth and sons.

al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: that is, "because he has," meaning: do not obey him for his wealth and his sons.

Ibn Amir, Abu Ja'far, al-Mughirah and Abu Haywah recited "an kana" with a single long hamzah, as an interrogative.

Hamzah, Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal recited "a-an kana" with two lightened hamzahs. The rest recited with a single hamzah as a statement. On the reading of the interrogative, the meaning is reproach and rebuke, since he repaid the blessings Allah had granted him of wealth and sons by disbelieving in Him and His Messenger.

Nafi', in one narration from him, recited it with a kasra on the hamzah, as a conditional.

﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Myths of the ancients."﴾ This is a new sentence functioning as an explanation of the prohibition. The meaning of "myths of the ancients" has been explained in several places earlier.

﴿We will brand him upon the snout﴾, that is, We will brand him with a mark on his snout.

Abu Ubaydah, Abu Zayd and al-Mubarrad said: al-khurtum is the nose.

Muqatil said: We will mark him with blackness on the nose, because his face will blacken before entering the Fire.

al-Farra' said: though the snout is specifically singled out for the mark, it is in the sense of the face, since part of the face stands for part of it.

al-Zajjaj said: a sign will be placed on him in the Hereafter by which the people of the Fire are recognized, through the blackening of their faces.

Qatadah said: We will attach to him something that never leaves him. Ibn Qutaybah chose this view and said: the Arabs say, "He has branded him with an evil brand," meaning that they attached to him a shame that never leaves him. So the meaning is that Allah attached to him a shame that never leaves him, like a mark on the snout. It was also said: the meaning of "We will brand him" is "We will strike him with the sword."

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: the meaning is "We will punish him for drinking wine," and wine is sometimes called al-kharTum (lit. "the snout"). From this is the saying of the poet:

"You spend your day in amusement and merriment, / and at night you are a drinker of the kharatim (wine-cups/wine)."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Saʿid ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-ʿAzama, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, narrated (it);

and Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat, al-Khatib in his Tarikh, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtara, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it, "Write!" It said, "O Lord, what shall I write?" He said, "Write the decree." So what is to be has flowed from that day until the Hour arises. Then the Record was folded up and the pen was lifted. His Throne was upon the water. The vapour of the water rose, and from it the heavens were split open. Then the Nun was created, and the earth was spread upon it, and the earth rests on the back of the Nun. The Nun moved, so the earth shook, and the mountains were set firm upon it, for the mountains boast over the earth until the Day of Resurrection. Then Ibn ʿAbbas recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿUbada ibn al-Samit, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it, 'Write!' So it wrote what is to be until eternity."

Ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of Muʿawiya ibn Qurra, from his father, with a marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet) report similar to it.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: God created the Nun, which is the inkwell, and created the pen, and said to it, "Write!" It said, "What shall I write?" He said, "Write what is to be until the Day of Resurrection."

al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi narrated from Abu Hurayra, marfuʿ, something similar.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Nun" is the inkwell.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The Nun is the fish upon which rests the earths, and the pen with which our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, wrote the decree, its good and its evil, its harm and its benefit." ﴿And what they inscribe﴾ — he said: "the noble scribes."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, narrated through several chains from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, that he said: "what they write."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, he said: "and what they know."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Muslim, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Saʿd ibn Hisham, who said: I came to ʿAisha and said, "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the character (khuluq) of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." She said: "His character was the Qur'an. Do you not read the Qur'an? ﴿Indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾."

Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nuʿaym in al-Dala'il, and al-Wahidi narrated from her, who said: "No one had better character than the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Whenever any of his companions or of his household called him, he would say, 'Labbayka' (here I am). For this reason God revealed: ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Abu al-Darda', who said: "ʿAisha was asked about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and she said: 'His character was the Qur'an: he was pleased with what pleases it, and angry at what angers it.'"

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Tirmidhi, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Jadali, who said: "I asked ʿAisha: 'What was the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)?' She said: 'He was not obscene nor given to obscenity, nor did he shout in the markets, nor did he repay evil with evil, but he pardoned and overlooked.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: ﴿So you will see and they will see﴾, he said: "You will know and they will know on the Day of Resurrection." ﴿Which of you is the afflicted (al-maftun)?﴾ He said: "The devil." They used to say, "He is a devil and he is a madman."

Ibn Jarir narrated from him concerning the verse: "Which of you is the madman (al-majnun)?"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him concerning His words: ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾, he said: "They wish you would grant them concessions, so they would grant you concessions."

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him concerning ﴿And do not obey every oath-swearing contemptible one﴾ up to the end of the verse, he said: "He means al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu ʿUthman al-Nahdi, who said: Marwan said, when the people pledged allegiance to Yazid: "It is the sunna of Abu Bakr and ʿUmar." ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said: "It is not the sunna of Abu Bakr and ʿUmar, but it is the sunna of Heraclius." Marwan said: "This is the one about whom was revealed: ﴿And he who said to his parents, 'Uff to you both!'﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 17], the verse..." ʿAisha heard that and said: "It was not revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Rahman, but it was revealed concerning your father: ﴿And do not obey every oath-swearing contemptible one, backbiting slanderer, going about with malicious talk﴾."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "There was revealed upon the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And do not obey every oath-swearing contemptible one, backbiting slanderer, going about with malicious talk﴾, and we did not know (who was meant) until there was revealed upon him: ﴿Besides all that, ignoble (zanim)﴾, and then we knew him: he had a mark like the wattle of a sheep."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: "The ʿutull is the illegitimately claimed (al-da'i), and the zanim is the suspicious one who is known for evil."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn ʿAsakir narrated from him: "The zanim is the da'i."

al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, narrated from him also: "The zanim is one known for evil, as a sheep is known by its wattle."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: "He is a man who passes by a people, and they say, 'A bad man.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him concerning His words ﴿zanim﴾: "He is oppressive (zalum)." It has also been said: these verses were revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, and it has been said: concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.

This surah is Makki according to al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata and Jabir.

It is reported from Ibn Abbas and Qatadah that from its beginning up to His words ﴿We will brand him upon the snout﴾ it is Makki (revealed in Makkah), and from after that up to His words ﴿among the righteous﴾ it is Madani (revealed in Madinah), and the rest of it is Makki. So said al-Mawardi.

Ibn al-Durays reported from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Whenever the opening of a surah was revealed in Makkah, it was written in Makkah, and then Allah added to it what He willed. The first of the Qur'an to be revealed was ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾, then ﴿Nun﴾, then al-Muzzammil, then al-Muddaththir."

al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi reported from him: "The surah of ﴿Nun﴾ was revealed in Makkah." Ibn Mardawayh reported the same from Aishah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His words ﴿Nun﴾: Abu Bakr, Warsh, Ibn Amir, al-Kisa'i, Ibn Muhaysin and Ibn Hubayrah recited it with idgham (assimilation, merging the second nun of its spelling into the waw), while the rest recited it with izhar (clear pronunciation). Abu Amr and Isa ibn Umar recited it with a fatha, on the basis of an implied verb.

Ibn Amir, Nasr and Ibn Ishaq recited it with a kasra, either on the basis of an implied oath or because of the meeting of two sakins (unvowelled letters). Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa' and Harun recited it with a damma, as an indeclinable form (bina').

Mujahid, Muqatil and al-Suddi said: it is the fish that carries the earth. Murrah al-Hamadhani, Ata al-Khurasani and al-Kalbi also said this.

It was also said that the nun is the last letter of the word al-Rahman.

Ibn Zayd said: it is an oath which Allah swore by.

Ibn Kaysan said: it is the opening of the surah.

Ata and Abu al-Aliyah said: it is the nun of nasr (help) and nasir (helper). Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Allah swore by His help to the believers.

It was also said: it is one of the letters of the alphabet, like the openings found at the beginnings of surahs that begin with such letters. We have already explained the correct view regarding such openings at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.

The waw in His words ﴿and the pen﴾ is the waw of oath: Allah swore by the pen because of what it contains of clarification (bayan). It applies to every pen with which something is written. A group of exegetes said: what is meant is the pen with which the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) was written, and Allah swore by it in glorification of it.

Qatadah said: the pen is among the blessings of Allah upon His servants.

﴿And what they inscribe﴾: "ma" here is a relative pronoun (mawsulah), meaning "and those who inscribe." The pronoun refers back to the people of the pen, who are indicated by its mention, since mention of the instrument of writing points to the writer.

The meaning is: "and those who inscribe," that is, who write everything that is written. Or it refers to the guardian angels (al-hafazah) mentioned earlier.

It is permissible for "ma" to be a verbal noun (masdariyyah), meaning "and their inscribing." It was also said that the pronoun refers to the pen alone, by way of attributing the verb to the instrument and treating it as though it were rational.

The answer to the oath is His words ﴿You are not, by the blessing of your Lord, a madman﴾. "Ma" is negating, "anta" is its subject, and "bi-majnun" is its predicate.

al-Zajjaj said: "anta" is the subject of "ma," "bi-majnun" is its predicate, and His words ﴿by the blessing of your Lord﴾ are a parenthetical statement placed in the middle. The meaning is: madness has been removed from you by the blessing of your Lord, just as one says "you are sane, by the praise of Allah."

It was said: the "ba" is attached to an implied word functioning as a circumstantial state (hal), as if it were said: "You are free of madness, connected to the blessing of Allah, which is prophethood and general leadership."

It was also said: the "ba" is for oath, meaning: "By you and the blessing of your Lord, you are not a madman."
