His saying ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾ is connected to the implied element in "lakum," meaning: they remain established for you until the Day of Resurrection, and We are not released from their obligation until We judge you on that Day. The answer to the oath is His saying: ﴿Indeed, for you is what you judge,﴾ because the meaning of ﴿Or do you have oaths﴾ is: "or have We sworn to you?"

Al-Razi said: The meaning is: "Or have We guaranteed to you and sworn to you with oaths that are emphatic and extreme in confirmation?"

It has also been said: the speech is complete at His saying "until the Day of Resurrection," and then He began: ﴿Indeed, for you is what you judge,﴾ meaning: the matter is not so.

The majority read "bali'ghah" (binding) in the nominative as an attribute of "aymān" (oaths). Al-Hasan and Zayd ibn Ali read it in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of "aymān," since it has become specified by its attribute, or as a qualifier of the pronoun in "lakum," or of the pronoun in "'alayna."

﴿Ask them, which of them stands surety for that?﴾ That is: Ask them, O Muhammad, rebuking and reproaching them: which of them guarantees for them, for this judgment that lies outside the right, that they will have in the Hereafter what the Muslims have.

Ibn Kaysan said: "al-za'im" (the surety) here means the one who undertakes the proof and the claim.

al-Hasan said: "al-za'im" is the Messenger.

﴿Or do they have associates?﴾ who share with them in this statement, agreeing with them about it. ﴿Then let them bring their associates, if they are truthful﴾ in what they claim. This is a command of incapacitation (amr ta'jiz), and the answer of the condition is omitted. It has been said: the meaning is: "Or do they have associates whom they make like the Muslims in the Hereafter?"

﴿The Day when a shin will be uncovered.﴾ "Yawma" is a temporal adverb governed by His saying "fal-ya'tu" (let them bring), meaning: let them bring them on the day when a shin is uncovered. It is also permissible for it to be a temporal adverb governed by an implied verb, meaning: remember the day when a shin is uncovered.

Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said regarding His saying ﴿'an saq﴾ (from a shin): it means "from a severity of the matter."

Ibn Qutaybah said: The origin of this is that a man, when he falls into a great matter that requires exertion in it, rolls up his shin (shammara 'an saqihi). So the uncovering of the shin is used metaphorically for a place of severity. He cited the verse of Durayd ibn al-Simmah:

"Short of garment, his half-shin protruding, patient in the ordeal, a climber of the Anjud."

He said: The interpretation of the verse is: the day when the matter becomes severe, just as the matter becomes severe when one needs to have the shin uncovered.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: When war or a matter grows intense, it is said: "the matter has uncovered its shin." The origin of this is that whoever falls into something that requires exertion rolls up his shin, so the shin and the uncovering are borrowed for the place of severity. Thus said others among the people of language, and the Arabs have used this in their poetry. Among that is the saying of the poet:

"The brother of war, if war bites him, bites it; and if war rolls up its shin, he rolls up (his)."

And the saying of another:

"And the horses run at the time of sunrise, and war has stood up with us on a shin."

And the saying of yet another:

"It has uncovered its shin, so tighten (your gear); and war has striven with you, so strive."

And the saying of yet another, about a year (of drought):

"It has uncovered its shin, reddish, stripping the flesh from its bones."

It has also been said: the "shin" of a thing is its root and its foundation, like the trunk of a tree and the shin of a man. That is: the day when the shin of the matter is uncovered, and its realities appear. It has also been said: it is uncovered from the shin of Hell. It has been said: from the shin of the Throne. It has been said: it is an expression for nearness. It has been said: the Lord, glory be to Him, uncovers His light. The truth of this will come at the end of the discussion. "And when the river of Allah comes, the river of Ma'qil is nullified."

The majority read "yakshifu" with the yā' (third person masculine), in the passive voice. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn Abi 'Ablah read "taksifu" with the tā' (feminine), in the active voice, meaning: the severity or the Hour (uncovers). It has also been read with the tā' in the passive voice, with the nūn, and with a tā' that is dammed with a kasra on the shin, from "uksifa al-amr," meaning: it has entered into uncovering.

﴿And they are called to prostration, but they will not be able.﴾ Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: all of creation will prostrate to Allah in one prostration, while the disbelievers and the hypocrites will remain, wanting to prostrate, but they will not be able to, because their spines will become stiff and not bend for prostration.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The veil will be removed, and those who believed in Allah in the world will fall and prostrate to Him. The others will be called to prostration, but they will not be able, because they had not believed in Allah in the world.

The accusative of ﴿humbled their eyes﴾ is a circumstantial qualifier (hal) from the pronoun in "yud'awna," and "abṣāruhum" is raised as the agent of it. The attribution of humility to the eyes is the abasement and humiliation, because its effect appears in them. ﴿Humiliation will cover them﴾ meaning: severe humiliation, remorse, and regret will overwhelm them. ﴿And they had been called to prostration﴾ meaning: in the world. ﴿while they were sound﴾ meaning: (p-1521) free from ailments, able to act.

Ibrahim al-Taymi said: They were called with the adhan and the iqamah, but they refused.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They hear "Hasten to success" (hayya 'ala al-falah) but do not answer.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: By Allah, this verse was not revealed except concerning those who stay away from the congregations.

It has also been said: they are called by the obligation that is directed at them by the Law, but they do not answer. The clause ﴿while they were sound﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial qualifier from the pronoun in "yud'awna."

﴿So leave Me with whoever denies this discourse.﴾ That is: leave Me to deal with him, and entrust his affair to Me, for I will suffice you against him.

al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is: do not let your heart be preoccupied with him; entrust him to Me, and I will suffice you concerning his affair.

The fa' is for the sequencing of what follows it from the command upon what precedes it. "Man" (whoever) is in the accusative by conjunction to the pronoun of the speaker, or as an object with "ma'a" (together with). The intended meaning of "this discourse" is the Qur'an, as al-Suddi said. It has been said: it means the Day of Resurrection. In this there is consolation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

The clause ﴿We will draw them on gradually from where they do not know﴾ is a new (resumptive) clause explaining the manner of their punishment, which is derived from His saying ﴿leave Me with whoever denies this discourse.﴾ The pronoun refers to "man" according to its meaning. The meaning is: We will seize them with punishment while they are heedless, and We will drive them to it step by step, until We bring them into it from where they do not know that this is istidraj (gradual drawing), because they think it is a favor and do not reflect on its outcome nor on what they will encounter at its end.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: He lavishes blessings upon them and makes them forget gratitude.

al-Hasan said: How many a one is drawn on gradually by being shown kindness, how many a one is tempted by being praised, and how many a one is deceived by being concealed (from consequences).

Istidraj (gradual drawing) is the leaving aside of hastening, and its origin is transfer from one state to another. It is said: istadraja fulan fulanan, meaning: he extracted what was with him little by little. It is said: darajahu ila kadha wa-istadrajahu, meaning: he brought him close to gradualness, so he became gradual.

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned that He gives respite to the wrongdoers, so He said: ﴿And I give them respite.﴾ That is: I give them time, so that they may increase in sin. The explanation of this has passed in the surahs al-A'raf and al-Tur. The root of "mala" is a period of time from the ages; it is said: Allah gave him respite (amla Allahu lahu), meaning: He lengthened the period for him. "Mala" (with the short vowel, maqsur) is the wide earth, named for its extension. ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm.﴾ That is: strong and severe, so nothing escapes Me. He, glory be to Him, called His kindness a plan (kayd), just as He called it istidraj, because it takes the form of a plan with regard to its outcome. He described it as firm (matin) for the strength of its effect in causing destruction.

﴿Or do you ask them for a reward?﴾ He, glory be to Him, returned the speech to what preceded in His saying: ﴿Or do they have associates?﴾ That is: Or do you seek from them a reward for what you call them to, of belief in Allah? ﴿Then they are burdened with a debt.﴾ Al-maghram means the penalty (gharamah), that is: they are burdened by the penalty of that reward, and "muthqalun" means: its carrying is heavy upon them because of their stinginess in spending wealth, so they turned away from answering you for this reason. The interrogation is for rebuke and reproach against them. The meaning is: you did not ask them that, and you did not seek it from them.

﴿Or is the unseen with them, so they write?﴾ That is: the Preserved Tablet, or everything that is hidden from them. So from that unseen they write what they want of proofs which they claim indicate their saying, and they dispute with you using what they write about that, and they judge for themselves what they want, and by that they dispense with answering you and complying with what you say.

﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord.﴾ That is: for His decree, which He has decreed in His foreknowledge. It has been said: the judgment here is His giving them respite and delaying the victory of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over them. It has been said: it is what He has decreed for him of conveying the message. It has been said: this is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword.

﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾ meaning Yunus, peace be upon him: do not be like him in anger, impatience, and haste. The adverbial clause in His saying ﴿when he called out﴾ is in the accusative governed by an implied genitive (mudaf mahdhuf), meaning: do not let your condition be like his condition at the time of his calling out. The clause ﴿while he was suppressed﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial qualifier from the doer of "nadā" (called out). Al-makzum means: filled with rage and distress.

Qatadah said: Indeed Allah consoles His Prophet ﷺ, and commands him to be patient and not to hurry as the companion of the fish hurried. The story of this has already been explained in the surahs al-Anbiya', Yunus, and al-Saffat. His calling out was with His saying: ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I was among the wrongdoers.﴾ (al-Anbiya': 87). It has also been said: al-makzum is one seized by his kazm, which is the passage of breath. This was said by al-Mubarrad. It has also been said: it is the one who is restrained. The first is preferable. From it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

"And you, from love of Mayy, conceal a sorrow, afflicted in heart, wounded in the heart, suppressed."

﴿Had not a blessing from his Lord overtaken him﴾ meaning: had it not been that a blessing from Allah overtook the companion of the fish, which was His granting him the guidance to repent, so Allah accepted his repentance. ﴿He would have been cast out onto the open waste﴾ meaning: he would have been thrown from the belly of the fish onto the surface of the earth, empty of vegetation, and he would have been blameworthy, meaning: he would have been censured and reproached for the sin he had committed, and expelled from mercy. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial qualifier from the pronoun in "nubidha."

Al-Dahhak said: The blessing here is prophethood.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It is his worship that had preceded.

Ibn Zayd said: it is his calling out with the words, ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 87]. It was also said: he was blameworthy and cast out.

It was also said: he was sinful.

The majority of reciters read ﴿تَدارَكَهُ﴾ (*tadarakahu*, "overtook him") in the past tense. Al-Hasan, Ibn Hurmuz and al-A'mash read it with a doubled *dal* (*tadarrakahu*). The original form is *tatadarraku*, a present-tense verb with two *ta'*s, and one of them was assimilated into the *dal*. This reading narrates the past situation as if it were present. Ubayy, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas read *tadarakat-hu* with the feminine *ta'* (*ta' al-ta'nith*), since the subject, *ni'mah* ("blessing"), is feminine.

﴿So his Lord chose him﴾: that is, He selected him, chose him, preferred him and appointed him for prophethood. ﴿And made him among the righteous﴾: that is, among those perfect in righteousness, and He protected him from sin. It was also said that He restored prophethood to him, made him an intercessor for himself and for his people, and sent him to a hundred thousand people or more, as has been mentioned previously.

﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you with their eyes﴾: *in* here is the light form of the heavy *inna* (*al-mukhaffafah min al-thaqilah*), i.e., *inna* with the *nun* lightened.

The majority read ﴿لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾ (*liyuzliqunaka*) with a *dammah* on the *ya'*, from *azlaqahu*, meaning "he made his foot slip," and it is said *azlaqahu 'an mawdi'ihi* when one moves him from his place. Nafi' and the people of Madinah read it with a *fathah* on the *ya'*, from *zalaqa 'an mawdi'ihi*, meaning he slipped or moved away from his place.

Al-Harawi said: that is, they would seize you by their evil eyes, so they would make you slip from your station, in which Allah established you, out of enmity toward you.

Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash, Mujahid and Abu Wa'il read ﴿لَيُرْهِقُونَكَ﴾ (*liyurhiqunaka*), meaning "they would destroy you."

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿يُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾ means they would turn you away from what you are upon, namely conveying the message. Al-Suddi and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said the same.

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl and al-Akhfash said: they would test you (*yaftinunaka*).

Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: they would kill you (*yaqtulunaka*).

Al-Zajjaj said: the view of the lexicographers regarding this verse is that, because of the intensity of their hatred and enmity, they nearly overthrow you with their gaze, which is a gaze of hatred. This is a common usage in speech: one says, "He looked at me with a look that nearly knocked me down, and a look that nearly devoured me."

Ibn Qutaybah said: Allah does not mean that they would afflict you with their eyes as the one who casts the evil eye afflicts what he admires with his eye. Rather, He means that when you recite the Qur'an they look at you with a fierce gaze full of enmity and hatred, which nearly brings you down, as the poet said:

*They clash with one another when they meet in an assembly,*
*with a gaze that removes the footing of feet.*

﴿When they hear the Reminder﴾: that is, at the time they hear the Qur'an, because of their extreme aversion to it. ﴿Lamma﴾ (*lamma*, "when") here is a temporal adverb in the accusative, governed by ﴿يُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾. It was also said that it is a particle, and its response is omitted because the preceding clause indicates it, meaning: when they hear the Reminder, they nearly slip you. ﴿And they say, "Indeed, he is mad"﴾: that is, they attribute madness to him whenever they hear him reciting the Qur'an.

Allah responded to them with His words: ﴿But it is not except a reminder to the worlds﴾. This sentence is either independent, or it is in the position of an accusative of circumstance (*hal*) relating to the subject of ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾, meaning: while the case is that it is a reminder and an explanation of everything they need, or an honor for them, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44]. It was also said that the pronoun refers to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): he is a reminder to the worlds, or an honor for them.

Al-Bukhari and others narrated from Abu Sa'id, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Our Lord will uncover His shin, and every believing man and woman will prostrate to Him. Those who used to prostrate in the world for show and reputation will remain, and they will go to prostrate, but their backs will become one solid plate." This hadith is established through several chains in the two Sahihs and others. It has versions, some of which are lengthy, and it is a well-known, famous hadith.

Ibn Mandah narrated from Abu Hurayrah regarding the verse, who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will uncover His shin.

'Abd al-Razzaq, 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mandah narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding the verse, who said: He will uncover His shin, blessed and exalted is He.

Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa al-Sifat* (who declared it weak), and Ibn 'Asakir narrated from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding the verse, that he said: "From a great light, and they will fall down prostrate to Him."

al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Mandah and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding the verse, who said: "It will be uncovered from a great matter." Then he said: "The war has stood upon a shin."

He said: Ibn Mas'ud said: He will uncover His shin, and every believer will prostrate, while the back of the disbeliever will become stiff and turn into one bone.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa al-Sifat* narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he was asked about the words of Allah, ﴿On the Day when the shin is uncovered﴾, and he said: "If something of the Qur'an is obscure to you, seek it in poetry, for it is the register of the Arabs. Have you not heard the words of the poet:"

*And the war stood with us upon a shin.*

Ibn 'Abbas said: "This is a day of severe distress." Something similar to this was narrated from him through other chains. Allah, glorified is He, has sufficed us in explaining this verse with what is authentically established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as you know, and that does not entail anthropomorphism or likening Allah to creation, for ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾.

*They left every statement in the presence of Muhammad's words,*
*and none believed in his religion like the one who ventured.*

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words, ﴿And they had been called to prostration while they were sound﴾, that he said: "They are the disbelievers who were called in the world while they were secure, but today they are called while they are fearful."

al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shu'ab* narrated from him regarding the verse, that he said: "A man hears the adhan but does not respond to the prayer."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him regarding His words, ﴿They would almost slip you with their eyes﴾, that he said: "They would pierce you with their eyes."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 68, verses 34–52 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, glory be to Him, finished mentioning the condition of the disbelievers, and comparing their trial to the trial of the people of the garden that was mentioned, He mentioned the condition of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) and the good that He has prepared for them.

He said: (p-1520) ﴿Indeed, for the God-fearing with their Lord are gardens of bliss.﴾ That is: for the God-fearing, who avoid what would incur His wrath, which is disbelief and sins, with Him, Mighty and Majestic, in the Hereafter, are gardens of pure bliss, which is not tainted by any turbidity and which is not troubled by the fear of its ending.

﴿Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals?﴾ The interrogation is for denial (istinkar).

The chieftains of the disbelievers of Quraysh saw that their share in this world was abundant while the share of the Muslims in it was small. When they heard the mention of the Hereafter and what Allah gives the Muslims in it, they said: "If what Muhammad claims is true, our condition and theirs will be nothing but like what it is in this world." So Allah, refuting them and rebutting them, said: ﴿Shall We then treat the Muslims...﴾ and so on. The fa' (then) here is for conjunction with an implied element, as is the case with its parallels.

Then Allah rebuked them, saying: ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ This crooked judgment, as if the matter of recompense were entrusted to you, so that you judge about it as you wish.

﴿Or do you have a Book in which you study?﴾ That is, you read in it and find that the obedient is like the disobedient. A similar statement is His, exalted is He: ﴿Or do you have a clear authority? So bring your Book.﴾ (al-Saffat: 156–157). Then He, glory be to Him, said: "Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose." The majority (al-jumhur) read "inna" with a kasra, considering it governed by "tadrusun" (you study), meaning: you study in the Book.

﴿Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose.﴾ When the lam entered, the hamza was given a kasra, as in His saying: "I know that you are indeed intelligent" (with kasra). Or it is by way of narrating what is studied, as in His saying: ﴿And We left for him among the later generations. Peace upon Noah among the worlds.﴾ (al-Saffat: 78–79). It has also been said: the speech is complete at His saying "tadrusun," and then He began: ﴿Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose﴾, meaning: you do not have that. Talhah ibn Musarrif and al-Dahhak read "anna lakum" with a fath on the hamza, considering the governing element to be "tadrusun" together with the addition of the emphatic lam. The meaning of "takhayyarun" is "you choose" and "you desire."

Then He, glory be to Him, increased the rebuke, saying: ﴿Or do you have oaths upon Us that are binding?﴾ That is: firm covenants, confirmed, secured, and extending to the utmost. The meaning is: Or do you have oaths upon Allah by which you have secured for yourselves that He will admit you to the Garden? His saying ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾ is connected to the implied element in "lakum," meaning: they remain established for you until the Day of Resurrection, and We are not released from their obligation until We judge you on that Day. The answer to the oath is His saying: ﴿Indeed, for you is what you judge,﴾ because the meaning of ﴿Or do you have oaths﴾ is: "or have We sworn to you?"

Al-Razi said: The meaning is: "Or have We guaranteed to you and sworn to you with oaths that are emphatic and extreme in confirmation?"

It has also been said: the speech is complete at His saying "until the Day of Resurrection," and then He began: ﴿Indeed, for you is what you judge,﴾ meaning: the matter is not so.

The majority read "bali'ghah" (binding) in the nominative as an attribute of "aymān" (oaths). Al-Hasan and Zayd ibn Ali read it in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of "aymān," since it has become specified by its attribute, or as a qualifier of the pronoun in "lakum," or of the pronoun in "'alayna."

﴿Ask them, which of them stands surety for that?﴾ That is: Ask them, O Muhammad, rebuking and reproaching them: which of them guarantees for them, for this judgment that lies outside the right, that they will have in the Hereafter what the Muslims have.

Ibn Kaysan said: "al-za'im" (the surety) here means the one who undertakes the proof and the claim.

al-Hasan said: "al-za'im" is the Messenger.

﴿Or do they have associates?﴾ who share with them in this statement, agreeing with them about it. ﴿Then let them bring their associates, if they are truthful﴾ in what they claim. This is a command of incapacitation (amr ta'jiz), and the answer of the condition is omitted. It has been said: the meaning is: "Or do they have associates whom they make like the Muslims in the Hereafter?"

﴿The Day when a shin will be uncovered.﴾ "Yawma" is a temporal adverb governed by His saying "fal-ya'tu" (let them bring), meaning: let them bring them on the day when a shin is uncovered. It is also permissible for it to be a temporal adverb governed by an implied verb, meaning: remember the day when a shin is uncovered.

Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said regarding His saying ﴿'an saq﴾ (from a shin): it means "from a severity of the matter."

Ibn Qutaybah said: The origin of this is that a man, when he falls into a great matter that requires exertion in it, rolls up his shin (shammara 'an saqihi). So the uncovering of the shin is used metaphorically for a place of severity. He cited the verse of Durayd ibn al-Simmah:

"Short of garment, his half-shin protruding, patient in the ordeal, a climber of the Anjud."

He said: The interpretation of the verse is: the day when the matter becomes severe, just as the matter becomes severe when one needs to have the shin uncovered.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: When war or a matter grows intense, it is said: "the matter has uncovered its shin." The origin of this is that whoever falls into something that requires exertion rolls up his shin, so the shin and the uncovering are borrowed for the place of severity. Thus said others among the people of language, and the Arabs have used this in their poetry. Among that is the saying of the poet:

"The brother of war, if war bites him, bites it; and if war rolls up its shin, he rolls up (his)."

And the saying of another:

"And the horses run at the time of sunrise, and war has stood up with us on a shin."

And the saying of yet another:

"It has uncovered its shin, so tighten (your gear); and war has striven with you, so strive."

And the saying of yet another, about a year (of drought):

"It has uncovered its shin, reddish, stripping the flesh from its bones."

It has also been said: the "shin" of a thing is its root and its foundation, like the trunk of a tree and the shin of a man. That is: the day when the shin of the matter is uncovered, and its realities appear. It has also been said: it is uncovered from the shin of Hell. It has been said: from the shin of the Throne. It has been said: it is an expression for nearness. It has been said: the Lord, glory be to Him, uncovers His light. The truth of this will come at the end of the discussion. "And when the river of Allah comes, the river of Ma'qil is nullified."

The majority read "yakshifu" with the yā' (third person masculine), in the passive voice. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn Abi 'Ablah read "taksifu" with the tā' (feminine), in the active voice, meaning: the severity or the Hour (uncovers). It has also been read with the tā' in the passive voice, with the nūn, and with a tā' that is dammed with a kasra on the shin, from "uksifa al-amr," meaning: it has entered into uncovering.

﴿And they are called to prostration, but they will not be able.﴾ Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: all of creation will prostrate to Allah in one prostration, while the disbelievers and the hypocrites will remain, wanting to prostrate, but they will not be able to, because their spines will become stiff and not bend for prostration.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The veil will be removed, and those who believed in Allah in the world will fall and prostrate to Him. The others will be called to prostration, but they will not be able, because they had not believed in Allah in the world.

The accusative of ﴿humbled their eyes﴾ is a circumstantial qualifier (hal) from the pronoun in "yud'awna," and "abṣāruhum" is raised as the agent of it. The attribution of humility to the eyes is the abasement and humiliation, because its effect appears in them. ﴿Humiliation will cover them﴾ meaning: severe humiliation, remorse, and regret will overwhelm them. ﴿And they had been called to prostration﴾ meaning: in the world. ﴿while they were sound﴾ meaning: (p-1521) free from ailments, able to act.

Ibrahim al-Taymi said: They were called with the adhan and the iqamah, but they refused.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They hear "Hasten to success" (hayya 'ala al-falah) but do not answer.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: By Allah, this verse was not revealed except concerning those who stay away from the congregations.

It has also been said: they are called by the obligation that is directed at them by the Law, but they do not answer. The clause ﴿while they were sound﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial qualifier from the pronoun in "yud'awna."

﴿So leave Me with whoever denies this discourse.﴾ That is: leave Me to deal with him, and entrust his affair to Me, for I will suffice you against him.

al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is: do not let your heart be preoccupied with him; entrust him to Me, and I will suffice you concerning his affair.

The fa' is for the sequencing of what follows it from the command upon what precedes it. "Man" (whoever) is in the accusative by conjunction to the pronoun of the speaker, or as an object with "ma'a" (together with). The intended meaning of "this discourse" is the Qur'an, as al-Suddi said. It has been said: it means the Day of Resurrection. In this there is consolation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

The clause ﴿We will draw them on gradually from where they do not know﴾ is a new (resumptive) clause explaining the manner of their punishment, which is derived from His saying ﴿leave Me with whoever denies this discourse.﴾ The pronoun refers to "man" according to its meaning. The meaning is: We will seize them with punishment while they are heedless, and We will drive them to it step by step, until We bring them into it from where they do not know that this is istidraj (gradual drawing), because they think it is a favor and do not reflect on its outcome nor on what they will encounter at its end.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: He lavishes blessings upon them and makes them forget gratitude.

al-Hasan said: How many a one is drawn on gradually by being shown kindness, how many a one is tempted by being praised, and how many a one is deceived by being concealed (from consequences).

Istidraj (gradual drawing) is the leaving aside of hastening, and its origin is transfer from one state to another. It is said: istadraja fulan fulanan, meaning: he extracted what was with him little by little. It is said: darajahu ila kadha wa-istadrajahu, meaning: he brought him close to gradualness, so he became gradual.

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned that He gives respite to the wrongdoers, so He said: ﴿And I give them respite.﴾ That is: I give them time, so that they may increase in sin. The explanation of this has passed in the surahs al-A'raf and al-Tur. The root of "mala" is a period of time from the ages; it is said: Allah gave him respite (amla Allahu lahu), meaning: He lengthened the period for him. "Mala" (with the short vowel, maqsur) is the wide earth, named for its extension. ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm.﴾ That is: strong and severe, so nothing escapes Me. He, glory be to Him, called His kindness a plan (kayd), just as He called it istidraj, because it takes the form of a plan with regard to its outcome. He described it as firm (matin) for the strength of its effect in causing destruction.

﴿Or do you ask them for a reward?﴾ He, glory be to Him, returned the speech to what preceded in His saying: ﴿Or do they have associates?﴾ That is: Or do you seek from them a reward for what you call them to, of belief in Allah? ﴿Then they are burdened with a debt.﴾ Al-maghram means the penalty (gharamah), that is: they are burdened by the penalty of that reward, and "muthqalun" means: its carrying is heavy upon them because of their stinginess in spending wealth, so they turned away from answering you for this reason. The interrogation is for rebuke and reproach against them. The meaning is: you did not ask them that, and you did not seek it from them.

﴿Or is the unseen with them, so they write?﴾ That is: the Preserved Tablet, or everything that is hidden from them. So from that unseen they write what they want of proofs which they claim indicate their saying, and they dispute with you using what they write about that, and they judge for themselves what they want, and by that they dispense with answering you and complying with what you say.

﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord.﴾ That is: for His decree, which He has decreed in His foreknowledge. It has been said: the judgment here is His giving them respite and delaying the victory of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over them. It has been said: it is what He has decreed for him of conveying the message. It has been said: this is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword.

﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾ meaning Yunus, peace be upon him: do not be like him in anger, impatience, and haste. The adverbial clause in His saying ﴿when he called out﴾ is in the accusative governed by an implied genitive (mudaf mahdhuf), meaning: do not let your condition be like his condition at the time of his calling out. The clause ﴿while he was suppressed﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial qualifier from the doer of "nadā" (called out). Al-makzum means: filled with rage and distress.

Qatadah said: Indeed Allah consoles His Prophet ﷺ, and commands him to be patient and not to hurry as the companion of the fish hurried. The story of this has already been explained in the surahs al-Anbiya', Yunus, and al-Saffat. His calling out was with His saying: ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I was among the wrongdoers.﴾ (al-Anbiya': 87). It has also been said: al-makzum is one seized by his kazm, which is the passage of breath. This was said by al-Mubarrad. It has also been said: it is the one who is restrained. The first is preferable. From it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

"And you, from love of Mayy, conceal a sorrow, afflicted in heart, wounded in the heart, suppressed."

﴿Had not a blessing from his Lord overtaken him﴾ meaning: had it not been that a blessing from Allah overtook the companion of the fish, which was His granting him the guidance to repent, so Allah accepted his repentance. ﴿He would have been cast out onto the open waste﴾ meaning: he would have been thrown from the belly of the fish onto the surface of the earth, empty of vegetation, and he would have been blameworthy, meaning: he would have been censured and reproached for the sin he had committed, and expelled from mercy. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial qualifier from the pronoun in "nubidha."

Al-Dahhak said: The blessing here is prophethood.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It is his worship that had preceded.

Ibn Zayd said: it is his calling out with the words, ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 87]. It was also said: he was blameworthy and cast out.

It was also said: he was sinful.

The majority of reciters read ﴿تَدارَكَهُ﴾ (*tadarakahu*, "overtook him") in the past tense. Al-Hasan, Ibn Hurmuz and al-A'mash read it with a doubled *dal* (*tadarrakahu*). The original form is *tatadarraku*, a present-tense verb with two *ta'*s, and one of them was assimilated into the *dal*. This reading narrates the past situation as if it were present. Ubayy, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas read *tadarakat-hu* with the feminine *ta'* (*ta' al-ta'nith*), since the subject, *ni'mah* ("blessing"), is feminine.

﴿So his Lord chose him﴾: that is, He selected him, chose him, preferred him and appointed him for prophethood. ﴿And made him among the righteous﴾: that is, among those perfect in righteousness, and He protected him from sin. It was also said that He restored prophethood to him, made him an intercessor for himself and for his people, and sent him to a hundred thousand people or more, as has been mentioned previously.

﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you with their eyes﴾: *in* here is the light form of the heavy *inna* (*al-mukhaffafah min al-thaqilah*), i.e., *inna* with the *nun* lightened.

The majority read ﴿لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾ (*liyuzliqunaka*) with a *dammah* on the *ya'*, from *azlaqahu*, meaning "he made his foot slip," and it is said *azlaqahu 'an mawdi'ihi* when one moves him from his place. Nafi' and the people of Madinah read it with a *fathah* on the *ya'*, from *zalaqa 'an mawdi'ihi*, meaning he slipped or moved away from his place.

Al-Harawi said: that is, they would seize you by their evil eyes, so they would make you slip from your station, in which Allah established you, out of enmity toward you.

Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash, Mujahid and Abu Wa'il read ﴿لَيُرْهِقُونَكَ﴾ (*liyurhiqunaka*), meaning "they would destroy you."

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿يُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾ means they would turn you away from what you are upon, namely conveying the message. Al-Suddi and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said the same.

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl and al-Akhfash said: they would test you (*yaftinunaka*).

Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: they would kill you (*yaqtulunaka*).

Al-Zajjaj said: the view of the lexicographers regarding this verse is that, because of the intensity of their hatred and enmity, they nearly overthrow you with their gaze, which is a gaze of hatred. This is a common usage in speech: one says, "He looked at me with a look that nearly knocked me down, and a look that nearly devoured me."

Ibn Qutaybah said: Allah does not mean that they would afflict you with their eyes as the one who casts the evil eye afflicts what he admires with his eye. Rather, He means that when you recite the Qur'an they look at you with a fierce gaze full of enmity and hatred, which nearly brings you down, as the poet said:

*They clash with one another when they meet in an assembly,*
*with a gaze that removes the footing of feet.*

﴿When they hear the Reminder﴾: that is, at the time they hear the Qur'an, because of their extreme aversion to it. ﴿Lamma﴾ (*lamma*, "when") here is a temporal adverb in the accusative, governed by ﴿يُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾. It was also said that it is a particle, and its response is omitted because the preceding clause indicates it, meaning: when they hear the Reminder, they nearly slip you. ﴿And they say, "Indeed, he is mad"﴾: that is, they attribute madness to him whenever they hear him reciting the Qur'an.

Allah responded to them with His words: ﴿But it is not except a reminder to the worlds﴾. This sentence is either independent, or it is in the position of an accusative of circumstance (*hal*) relating to the subject of ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾, meaning: while the case is that it is a reminder and an explanation of everything they need, or an honor for them, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44]. It was also said that the pronoun refers to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): he is a reminder to the worlds, or an honor for them.

Al-Bukhari and others narrated from Abu Sa'id, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Our Lord will uncover His shin, and every believing man and woman will prostrate to Him. Those who used to prostrate in the world for show and reputation will remain, and they will go to prostrate, but their backs will become one solid plate." This hadith is established through several chains in the two Sahihs and others. It has versions, some of which are lengthy, and it is a well-known, famous hadith.

Ibn Mandah narrated from Abu Hurayrah regarding the verse, who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will uncover His shin.

'Abd al-Razzaq, 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mandah narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding the verse, who said: He will uncover His shin, blessed and exalted is He.

Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa al-Sifat* (who declared it weak), and Ibn 'Asakir narrated from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding the verse, that he said: "From a great light, and they will fall down prostrate to Him."

al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Mandah and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding the verse, who said: "It will be uncovered from a great matter." Then he said: "The war has stood upon a shin."

He said: Ibn Mas'ud said: He will uncover His shin, and every believer will prostrate, while the back of the disbeliever will become stiff and turn into one bone.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa al-Sifat* narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he was asked about the words of Allah, ﴿On the Day when the shin is uncovered﴾, and he said: "If something of the Qur'an is obscure to you, seek it in poetry, for it is the register of the Arabs. Have you not heard the words of the poet:"

*And the war stood with us upon a shin.*

Ibn 'Abbas said: "This is a day of severe distress." Something similar to this was narrated from him through other chains. Allah, glorified is He, has sufficed us in explaining this verse with what is authentically established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as you know, and that does not entail anthropomorphism or likening Allah to creation, for ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾.

*They left every statement in the presence of Muhammad's words,*
*and none believed in his religion like the one who ventured.*

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words, ﴿And they had been called to prostration while they were sound﴾, that he said: "They are the disbelievers who were called in the world while they were secure, but today they are called while they are fearful."

al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shu'ab* narrated from him regarding the verse, that he said: "A man hears the adhan but does not respond to the prayer."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him regarding His words, ﴿They would almost slip you with their eyes﴾, that he said: "They would pierce you with their eyes."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 68, verses 34–52 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, glory be to Him, finished mentioning the condition of the disbelievers, and comparing their trial to the trial of the people of the garden that was mentioned, He mentioned the condition of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) and the good that He has prepared for them.

He said: (p-1520) ﴿Indeed, for the God-fearing with their Lord are gardens of bliss.﴾ That is: for the God-fearing, who avoid what would incur His wrath, which is disbelief and sins, with Him, Mighty and Majestic, in the Hereafter, are gardens of pure bliss, which is not tainted by any turbidity and which is not troubled by the fear of its ending.

﴿Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals?﴾ The interrogation is for denial (istinkar).

The chieftains of the disbelievers of Quraysh saw that their share in this world was abundant while the share of the Muslims in it was small. When they heard the mention of the Hereafter and what Allah gives the Muslims in it, they said: "If what Muhammad claims is true, our condition and theirs will be nothing but like what it is in this world." So Allah, refuting them and rebutting them, said: ﴿Shall We then treat the Muslims...﴾ and so on. The fa' (then) here is for conjunction with an implied element, as is the case with its parallels.

Then Allah rebuked them, saying: ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ This crooked judgment, as if the matter of recompense were entrusted to you, so that you judge about it as you wish.

﴿Or do you have a Book in which you study?﴾ That is, you read in it and find that the obedient is like the disobedient. A similar statement is His, exalted is He: ﴿Or do you have a clear authority? So bring your Book.﴾ (al-Saffat: 156–157). Then He, glory be to Him, said: "Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose." The majority (al-jumhur) read "inna" with a kasra, considering it governed by "tadrusun" (you study), meaning: you study in the Book.

﴿Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose.﴾ When the lam entered, the hamza was given a kasra, as in His saying: "I know that you are indeed intelligent" (with kasra). Or it is by way of narrating what is studied, as in His saying: ﴿And We left for him among the later generations. Peace upon Noah among the worlds.﴾ (al-Saffat: 78–79). It has also been said: the speech is complete at His saying "tadrusun," and then He began: ﴿Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose﴾, meaning: you do not have that. Talhah ibn Musarrif and al-Dahhak read "anna lakum" with a fath on the hamza, considering the governing element to be "tadrusun" together with the addition of the emphatic lam. The meaning of "takhayyarun" is "you choose" and "you desire."

Then He, glory be to Him, increased the rebuke, saying: ﴿Or do you have oaths upon Us that are binding?﴾ That is: firm covenants, confirmed, secured, and extending to the utmost. The meaning is: Or do you have oaths upon Allah by which you have secured for yourselves that He will admit you to the Garden? His saying ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾ is connected to the implied element in "lakum," meaning: they remain established for you until the Day of Resurrection, and We are not released from their obligation until We judge you on that Day. The answer to the oath is His saying: ﴿Indeed, for you is what you judge,﴾ because the meaning of ﴿Or do you have oaths﴾ is: "or have We sworn to you?"

Al-Razi said: The meaning is: "Or have We guaranteed to you and sworn to you with oaths that are emphatic and extreme in confirmation?"

It has also been said: the speech is complete at His saying "until the Day of Resurrection," and then He began: ﴿Indeed, for you is what you judge,﴾ meaning: the matter is not so.

The majority read "bali'ghah" (binding) in the nominative as an attribute of "aymān" (oaths). Al-Hasan and Zayd ibn Ali read it in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of "aymān," since it has become specified by its attribute, or as a qualifier of the pronoun in "lakum," or of the pronoun in "'alayna."

﴿Ask them, which of them stands surety for that?﴾ That is: Ask them, O Muhammad, rebuking and reproaching them: which of them guarantees for them, for this judgment that lies outside the right, that they will have in the Hereafter what the Muslims have.

Ibn Kaysan said: "al-za'im" (the surety) here means the one who undertakes the proof and the claim.

al-Hasan said: "al-za'im" is the Messenger.

﴿Or do they have associates?﴾ who share with them in this statement, agreeing with them about it. ﴿Then let them bring their associates, if they are truthful﴾ in what they claim. This is a command of incapacitation (amr ta'jiz), and the answer of the condition is omitted. It has been said: the meaning is: "Or do they have associates whom they make like the Muslims in the Hereafter?"

﴿The Day when a shin will be uncovered.﴾ "Yawma" is a temporal adverb governed by His saying "fal-ya'tu" (let them bring), meaning: let them bring them on the day when a shin is uncovered. It is also permissible for it to be a temporal adverb governed by an implied verb, meaning: remember the day when a shin is uncovered.

Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said regarding His saying ﴿'an saq﴾ (from a shin): it means "from a severity of the matter."

Ibn Qutaybah said: The origin of this is that a man, when he falls into a great matter that requires exertion in it, rolls up his shin (shammara 'an saqihi). So the uncovering of the shin is used metaphorically for a place of severity. He cited the verse of Durayd ibn al-Simmah:

"Short of garment, his half-shin protruding, patient in the ordeal, a climber of the Anjud."

He said: The interpretation of the verse is: the day when the matter becomes severe, just as the matter becomes severe when one needs to have the shin uncovered.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: When war or a matter grows intense, it is said: "the matter has uncovered its shin." The origin of this is that whoever falls into something that requires exertion rolls up his shin, so the shin and the uncovering are borrowed for the place of severity. Thus said others among the people of language, and the Arabs have used this in their poetry. Among that is the saying of the poet:

"The brother of war, if war bites him, bites it; and if war rolls up its shin, he rolls up (his)."

And the saying of another:

"And the horses run at the time of sunrise, and war has stood up with us on a shin."

And the saying of yet another:

"It has uncovered its shin, so tighten (your gear); and war has striven with you, so strive."

And the saying of yet another, about a year (of drought):

"It has uncovered its shin, reddish, stripping the flesh from its bones."

It has also been said: the "shin" of a thing is its root and its foundation, like the trunk of a tree and the shin of a man. That is: the day when the shin of the matter is uncovered, and its realities appear. It has also been said: it is uncovered from the shin of Hell. It has been said: from the shin of the Throne. It has been said: it is an expression for nearness. It has been said: the Lord, glory be to Him, uncovers His light. The truth of this will come at the end of the discussion. "And when the river of Allah comes, the river of Ma'qil is nullified."

The majority read "yakshifu" with the yā' (third person masculine), in the passive voice. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn Abi 'Ablah read "taksifu" with the tā' (feminine), in the active voice, meaning: the severity or the Hour (uncovers). It has also been read with the tā' in the passive voice, with the nūn, and with a tā' that is dammed with a kasra on the shin, from "uksifa al-amr," meaning: it has entered into uncovering.

﴿And they are called to prostration, but they will not be able.﴾ Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: all of creation will prostrate to Allah in one prostration, while the disbelievers and the hypocrites will remain, wanting to prostrate, but they will not be able to, because their spines will become stiff and not bend for prostration.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The veil will be removed, and those who believed in Allah in the world will fall and prostrate to Him. The others will be called to prostration, but they will not be able, because they had not believed in Allah in the world.

The accusative of ﴿humbled their eyes﴾ is a circumstantial qualifier (hal) from the pronoun in "yud'awna," and "abṣāruhum" is raised as the agent of it. The attribution of humility to the eyes is the abasement and humiliation, because its effect appears in them. ﴿Humiliation will cover them﴾ meaning: severe humiliation, remorse, and regret will overwhelm them. ﴿And they had been called to prostration﴾ meaning: in the world. ﴿while they were sound﴾ meaning: (p-1521) free from ailments, able to act.

Ibrahim al-Taymi said: They were called with the adhan and the iqamah, but they refused.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They hear "Hasten to success" (hayya 'ala al-falah) but do not answer.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: By Allah, this verse was not revealed except concerning those who stay away from the congregations.

It has also been said: they are called by the obligation that is directed at them by the Law, but they do not answer. The clause ﴿while they were sound﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial qualifier from the pronoun in "yud'awna."

﴿So leave Me with whoever denies this discourse.﴾ That is: leave Me to deal with him, and entrust his affair to Me, for I will suffice you against him.

al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is: do not let your heart be preoccupied with him; entrust him to Me, and I will suffice you concerning his affair.

The fa' is for the sequencing of what follows it from the command upon what precedes it. "Man" (whoever) is in the accusative by conjunction to the pronoun of the speaker, or as an object with "ma'a" (together with). The intended meaning of "this discourse" is the Qur'an, as al-Suddi said. It has been said: it means the Day of Resurrection. In this there is consolation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

The clause ﴿We will draw them on gradually from where they do not know﴾ is a new (resumptive) clause explaining the manner of their punishment, which is derived from His saying ﴿leave Me with whoever denies this discourse.﴾ The pronoun refers to "man" according to its meaning. The meaning is: We will seize them with punishment while they are heedless, and We will drive them to it step by step, until We bring them into it from where they do not know that this is istidraj (gradual drawing), because they think it is a favor and do not reflect on its outcome nor on what they will encounter at its end.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: He lavishes blessings upon them and makes them forget gratitude.

al-Hasan said: How many a one is drawn on gradually by being shown kindness, how many a one is tempted by being praised, and how many a one is deceived by being concealed (from consequences).

Istidraj (gradual drawing) is the leaving aside of hastening, and its origin is transfer from one state to another. It is said: istadraja fulan fulanan, meaning: he extracted what was with him little by little. It is said: darajahu ila kadha wa-istadrajahu, meaning: he brought him close to gradualness, so he became gradual.

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned that He gives respite to the wrongdoers, so He said: ﴿And I give them respite.﴾ That is: I give them time, so that they may increase in sin. The explanation of this has passed in the surahs al-A'raf and al-Tur. The root of "mala" is a period of time from the ages; it is said: Allah gave him respite (amla Allahu lahu), meaning: He lengthened the period for him. "Mala" (with the short vowel, maqsur) is the wide earth, named for its extension. ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm.﴾ That is: strong and severe, so nothing escapes Me. He, glory be to Him, called His kindness a plan (kayd), just as He called it istidraj, because it takes the form of a plan with regard to its outcome. He described it as firm (matin) for the strength of its effect in causing destruction.

﴿Or do you ask them for a reward?﴾ He, glory be to Him, returned the speech to what preceded in His saying: ﴿Or do they have associates?﴾ That is: Or do you seek from them a reward for what you call them to, of belief in Allah? ﴿Then they are burdened with a debt.﴾ Al-maghram means the penalty (gharamah), that is: they are burdened by the penalty of that reward, and "muthqalun" means: its carrying is heavy upon them because of their stinginess in spending wealth, so they turned away from answering you for this reason. The interrogation is for rebuke and reproach against them. The meaning is: you did not ask them that, and you did not seek it from them.

﴿Or is the unseen with them, so they write?﴾ That is: the Preserved Tablet, or everything that is hidden from them. So from that unseen they write what they want of proofs which they claim indicate their saying, and they dispute with you using what they write about that, and they judge for themselves what they want, and by that they dispense with answering you and complying with what you say.

﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord.﴾ That is: for His decree, which He has decreed in His foreknowledge. It has been said: the judgment here is His giving them respite and delaying the victory of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over them. It has been said: it is what He has decreed for him of conveying the message. It has been said: this is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword.

﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾ meaning Yunus, peace be upon him: do not be like him in anger, impatience, and haste. The adverbial clause in His saying ﴿when he called out﴾ is in the accusative governed by an implied genitive (mudaf mahdhuf), meaning: do not let your condition be like his condition at the time of his calling out. The clause ﴿while he was suppressed﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial qualifier from the doer of "nadā" (called out). Al-makzum means: filled with rage and distress.

Qatadah said: Indeed Allah consoles His Prophet ﷺ, and commands him to be patient and not to hurry as the companion of the fish hurried. The story of this has already been explained in the surahs al-Anbiya', Yunus, and al-Saffat. His calling out was with His saying: ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I was among the wrongdoers.﴾ (al-Anbiya': 87). It has also been said: al-makzum is one seized by his kazm, which is the passage of breath. This was said by al-Mubarrad. It has also been said: it is the one who is restrained. The first is preferable. From it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

"And you, from love of Mayy, conceal a sorrow, afflicted in heart, wounded in the heart, suppressed."

﴿Had not a blessing from his Lord overtaken him﴾ meaning: had it not been that a blessing from Allah overtook the companion of the fish, which was His granting him the guidance to repent, so Allah accepted his repentance. ﴿He would have been cast out onto the open waste﴾ meaning: he would have been thrown from the belly of the fish onto the surface of the earth, empty of vegetation, and he would have been blameworthy, meaning: he would have been censured and reproached for the sin he had committed, and expelled from mercy. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial qualifier from the pronoun in "nubidha."

Al-Dahhak said: The blessing here is prophethood.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It is his worship that had preceded.

Ibn Zayd said: it is his calling out with the words, ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 87]. It was also said: he was blameworthy and cast out.

It was also said: he was sinful.

The majority of reciters read ﴿تَدارَكَهُ﴾ (*tadarakahu*, "overtook him") in the past tense. Al-Hasan, Ibn Hurmuz and al-A'mash read it with a doubled *dal* (*tadarrakahu*). The original form is *tatadarraku*, a present-tense verb with two *ta'*s, and one of them was assimilated into the *dal*. This reading narrates the past situation as if it were present. Ubayy, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas read *tadarakat-hu* with the feminine *ta'* (*ta' al-ta'nith*), since the subject, *ni'mah* ("blessing"), is feminine.

﴿So his Lord chose him﴾: that is, He selected him, chose him, preferred him and appointed him for prophethood. ﴿And made him among the righteous﴾: that is, among those perfect in righteousness, and He protected him from sin. It was also said that He restored prophethood to him, made him an intercessor for himself and for his people, and sent him to a hundred thousand people or more, as has been mentioned previously.

﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you with their eyes﴾: *in* here is the light form of the heavy *inna* (*al-mukhaffafah min al-thaqilah*), i.e., *inna* with the *nun* lightened.

The majority read ﴿لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾ (*liyuzliqunaka*) with a *dammah* on the *ya'*, from *azlaqahu*, meaning "he made his foot slip," and it is said *azlaqahu 'an mawdi'ihi* when one moves him from his place. Nafi' and the people of Madinah read it with a *fathah* on the *ya'*, from *zalaqa 'an mawdi'ihi*, meaning he slipped or moved away from his place.

Al-Harawi said: that is, they would seize you by their evil eyes, so they would make you slip from your station, in which Allah established you, out of enmity toward you.

Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash, Mujahid and Abu Wa'il read ﴿لَيُرْهِقُونَكَ﴾ (*liyurhiqunaka*), meaning "they would destroy you."

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿يُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾ means they would turn you away from what you are upon, namely conveying the message. Al-Suddi and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said the same.

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl and al-Akhfash said: they would test you (*yaftinunaka*).

Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: they would kill you (*yaqtulunaka*).

Al-Zajjaj said: the view of the lexicographers regarding this verse is that, because of the intensity of their hatred and enmity, they nearly overthrow you with their gaze, which is a gaze of hatred. This is a common usage in speech: one says, "He looked at me with a look that nearly knocked me down, and a look that nearly devoured me."

Ibn Qutaybah said: Allah does not mean that they would afflict you with their eyes as the one who casts the evil eye afflicts what he admires with his eye. Rather, He means that when you recite the Qur'an they look at you with a fierce gaze full of enmity and hatred, which nearly brings you down, as the poet said:

*They clash with one another when they meet in an assembly,*
*with a gaze that removes the footing of feet.*

﴿When they hear the Reminder﴾: that is, at the time they hear the Qur'an, because of their extreme aversion to it. ﴿Lamma﴾ (*lamma*, "when") here is a temporal adverb in the accusative, governed by ﴿يُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾. It was also said that it is a particle, and its response is omitted because the preceding clause indicates it, meaning: when they hear the Reminder, they nearly slip you. ﴿And they say, "Indeed, he is mad"﴾: that is, they attribute madness to him whenever they hear him reciting the Qur'an.

Allah responded to them with His words: ﴿But it is not except a reminder to the worlds﴾. This sentence is either independent, or it is in the position of an accusative of circumstance (*hal*) relating to the subject of ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾, meaning: while the case is that it is a reminder and an explanation of everything they need, or an honor for them, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44]. It was also said that the pronoun refers to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): he is a reminder to the worlds, or an honor for them.

Al-Bukhari and others narrated from Abu Sa'id, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Our Lord will uncover His shin, and every believing man and woman will prostrate to Him. Those who used to prostrate in the world for show and reputation will remain, and they will go to prostrate, but their backs will become one solid plate." This hadith is established through several chains in the two Sahihs and others. It has versions, some of which are lengthy, and it is a well-known, famous hadith.

Ibn Mandah narrated from Abu Hurayrah regarding the verse, who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will uncover His shin.

'Abd al-Razzaq, 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mandah narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding the verse, who said: He will uncover His shin, blessed and exalted is He.

Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa al-Sifat* (who declared it weak), and Ibn 'Asakir narrated from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding the verse, that he said: "From a great light, and they will fall down prostrate to Him."

al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Mandah and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding the verse, who said: "It will be uncovered from a great matter." Then he said: "The war has stood upon a shin."

He said: Ibn Mas'ud said: He will uncover His shin, and every believer will prostrate, while the back of the disbeliever will become stiff and turn into one bone.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa al-Sifat* narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he was asked about the words of Allah, ﴿On the Day when the shin is uncovered﴾, and he said: "If something of the Qur'an is obscure to you, seek it in poetry, for it is the register of the Arabs. Have you not heard the words of the poet:"

*And the war stood with us upon a shin.*

Ibn 'Abbas said: "This is a day of severe distress." Something similar to this was narrated from him through other chains. Allah, glorified is He, has sufficed us in explaining this verse with what is authentically established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as you know, and that does not entail anthropomorphism or likening Allah to creation, for ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾.

*They left every statement in the presence of Muhammad's words,*
*and none believed in his religion like the one who ventured.*

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words, ﴿And they had been called to prostration while they were sound﴾, that he said: "They are the disbelievers who were called in the world while they were secure, but today they are called while they are fearful."

al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shu'ab* narrated from him regarding the verse, that he said: "A man hears the adhan but does not respond to the prayer."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him regarding His words, ﴿They would almost slip you with their eyes﴾, that he said: "They would pierce you with their eyes."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 68, verses 34–52 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, glory be to Him, finished mentioning the condition of the disbelievers, and comparing their trial to the trial of the people of the garden that was mentioned, He mentioned the condition of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) and the good that He has prepared for them.

He said: (p-1520) ﴿Indeed, for the God-fearing with their Lord are gardens of bliss.﴾ That is: for the God-fearing, who avoid what would incur His wrath, which is disbelief and sins, with Him, Mighty and Majestic, in the Hereafter, are gardens of pure bliss, which is not tainted by any turbidity and which is not troubled by the fear of its ending.

﴿Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals?﴾ The interrogation is for denial (istinkar).

The chieftains of the disbelievers of Quraysh saw that their share in this world was abundant while the share of the Muslims in it was small. When they heard the mention of the Hereafter and what Allah gives the Muslims in it, they said: "If what Muhammad claims is true, our condition and theirs will be nothing but like what it is in this world." So Allah, refuting them and rebutting them, said: ﴿Shall We then treat the Muslims...﴾ and so on. The fa' (then) here is for conjunction with an implied element, as is the case with its parallels.

Then Allah rebuked them, saying: ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ This crooked judgment, as if the matter of recompense were entrusted to you, so that you judge about it as you wish.

﴿Or do you have a Book in which you study?﴾ That is, you read in it and find that the obedient is like the disobedient. A similar statement is His, exalted is He: ﴿Or do you have a clear authority? So bring your Book.﴾ (al-Saffat: 156–157). Then He, glory be to Him, said: "Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose." The majority (al-jumhur) read "inna" with a kasra, considering it governed by "tadrusun" (you study), meaning: you study in the Book.

﴿Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose.﴾ When the lam entered, the hamza was given a kasra, as in His saying: "I know that you are indeed intelligent" (with kasra). Or it is by way of narrating what is studied, as in His saying: ﴿And We left for him among the later generations. Peace upon Noah among the worlds.﴾ (al-Saffat: 78–79). It has also been said: the speech is complete at His saying "tadrusun," and then He began: ﴿Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose﴾, meaning: you do not have that. Talhah ibn Musarrif and al-Dahhak read "anna lakum" with a fath on the hamza, considering the governing element to be "tadrusun" together with the addition of the emphatic lam. The meaning of "takhayyarun" is "you choose" and "you desire."

Then He, glory be to Him, increased the rebuke, saying: ﴿Or do you have oaths upon Us that are binding?﴾ That is: firm covenants, confirmed, secured, and extending to the utmost. The meaning is: Or do you have oaths upon Allah by which you have secured for yourselves that He will admit you to the Garden? His saying ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾ is connected to the implied element in "lakum," meaning: they remain established for you until the Day of Resurrection, and We are not released from their obligation until We judge you on that Day. The answer to the oath is His saying: ﴿Indeed, for you is what you judge,﴾ because the meaning of ﴿Or do you have oaths﴾ is: "or have We sworn to you?"

Al-Razi said: The meaning is: "Or have We guaranteed to you and sworn to you with oaths that are emphatic and extreme in confirmation?"

It has also been said: the speech is complete at His saying "until the Day of Resurrection," and then He began: ﴿Indeed, for you is what you judge,﴾ meaning: the matter is not so.

The majority read "bali'ghah" (binding) in the nominative as an attribute of "aymān" (oaths). Al-Hasan and Zayd ibn Ali read it in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of "aymān," since it has become specified by its attribute, or as a qualifier of the pronoun in "lakum," or of the pronoun in "'alayna."

﴿Ask them, which of them stands surety for that?﴾ That is: Ask them, O Muhammad, rebuking and reproaching them: which of them guarantees for them, for this judgment that lies outside the right, that they will have in the Hereafter what the Muslims have.

Ibn Kaysan said: "al-za'im" (the surety) here means the one who undertakes the proof and the claim.

al-Hasan said: "al-za'im" is the Messenger.

﴿Or do they have associates?﴾ who share with them in this statement, agreeing with them about it. ﴿Then let them bring their associates, if they are truthful﴾ in what they claim. This is a command of incapacitation (amr ta'jiz), and the answer of the condition is omitted. It has been said: the meaning is: "Or do they have associates whom they make like the Muslims in the Hereafter?"

﴿The Day when a shin will be uncovered.﴾ "Yawma" is a temporal adverb governed by His saying "fal-ya'tu" (let them bring), meaning: let them bring them on the day when a shin is uncovered. It is also permissible for it to be a temporal adverb governed by an implied verb, meaning: remember the day when a shin is uncovered.

Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said regarding His saying ﴿'an saq﴾ (from a shin): it means "from a severity of the matter."

Ibn Qutaybah said: The origin of this is that a man, when he falls into a great matter that requires exertion in it, rolls up his shin (shammara 'an saqihi). So the uncovering of the shin is used metaphorically for a place of severity. He cited the verse of Durayd ibn al-Simmah:

"Short of garment, his half-shin protruding, patient in the ordeal, a climber of the Anjud."

He said: The interpretation of the verse is: the day when the matter becomes severe, just as the matter becomes severe when one needs to have the shin uncovered.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: When war or a matter grows intense, it is said: "the matter has uncovered its shin." The origin of this is that whoever falls into something that requires exertion rolls up his shin, so the shin and the uncovering are borrowed for the place of severity. Thus said others among the people of language, and the Arabs have used this in their poetry. Among that is the saying of the poet:

"The brother of war, if war bites him, bites it; and if war rolls up its shin, he rolls up (his)."

And the saying of another:

"And the horses run at the time of sunrise, and war has stood up with us on a shin."

And the saying of yet another:

"It has uncovered its shin, so tighten (your gear); and war has striven with you, so strive."

And the saying of yet another, about a year (of drought):

"It has uncovered its shin, reddish, stripping the flesh from its bones."

It has also been said: the "shin" of a thing is its root and its foundation, like the trunk of a tree and the shin of a man. That is: the day when the shin of the matter is uncovered, and its realities appear. It has also been said: it is uncovered from the shin of Hell. It has been said: from the shin of the Throne. It has been said: it is an expression for nearness. It has been said: the Lord, glory be to Him, uncovers His light. The truth of this will come at the end of the discussion. "And when the river of Allah comes, the river of Ma'qil is nullified."

The majority read "yakshifu" with the yā' (third person masculine), in the passive voice. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn Abi 'Ablah read "taksifu" with the tā' (feminine), in the active voice, meaning: the severity or the Hour (uncovers). It has also been read with the tā' in the passive voice, with the nūn, and with a tā' that is dammed with a kasra on the shin, from "uksifa al-amr," meaning: it has entered into uncovering.

﴿And they are called to prostration, but they will not be able.﴾ Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: all of creation will prostrate to Allah in one prostration, while the disbelievers and the hypocrites will remain, wanting to prostrate, but they will not be able to, because their spines will become stiff and not bend for prostration.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The veil will be removed, and those who believed in Allah in the world will fall and prostrate to Him. The others will be called to prostration, but they will not be able, because they had not believed in Allah in the world.

The accusative of ﴿humbled their eyes﴾ is a circumstantial qualifier (hal) from the pronoun in "yud'awna," and "abṣāruhum" is raised as the agent of it. The attribution of humility to the eyes is the abasement and humiliation, because its effect appears in them. ﴿Humiliation will cover them﴾ meaning: severe humiliation, remorse, and regret will overwhelm them. ﴿And they had been called to prostration﴾ meaning: in the world. ﴿while they were sound﴾ meaning: (p-1521) free from ailments, able to act.

Ibrahim al-Taymi said: They were called with the adhan and the iqamah, but they refused.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They hear "Hasten to success" (hayya 'ala al-falah) but do not answer.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: By Allah, this verse was not revealed except concerning those who stay away from the congregations.

It has also been said: they are called by the obligation that is directed at them by the Law, but they do not answer. The clause ﴿while they were sound﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial qualifier from the pronoun in "yud'awna."

﴿So leave Me with whoever denies this discourse.﴾ That is: leave Me to deal with him, and entrust his affair to Me, for I will suffice you against him.

al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is: do not let your heart be preoccupied with him; entrust him to Me, and I will suffice you concerning his affair.

The fa' is for the sequencing of what follows it from the command upon what precedes it. "Man" (whoever) is in the accusative by conjunction to the pronoun of the speaker, or as an object with "ma'a" (together with). The intended meaning of "this discourse" is the Qur'an, as al-Suddi said. It has been said: it means the Day of Resurrection. In this there is consolation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

The clause ﴿We will draw them on gradually from where they do not know﴾ is a new (resumptive) clause explaining the manner of their punishment, which is derived from His saying ﴿leave Me with whoever denies this discourse.﴾ The pronoun refers to "man" according to its meaning. The meaning is: We will seize them with punishment while they are heedless, and We will drive them to it step by step, until We bring them into it from where they do not know that this is istidraj (gradual drawing), because they think it is a favor and do not reflect on its outcome nor on what they will encounter at its end.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: He lavishes blessings upon them and makes them forget gratitude.

al-Hasan said: How many a one is drawn on gradually by being shown kindness, how many a one is tempted by being praised, and how many a one is deceived by being concealed (from consequences).

Istidraj (gradual drawing) is the leaving aside of hastening, and its origin is transfer from one state to another. It is said: istadraja fulan fulanan, meaning: he extracted what was with him little by little. It is said: darajahu ila kadha wa-istadrajahu, meaning: he brought him close to gradualness, so he became gradual.

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned that He gives respite to the wrongdoers, so He said: ﴿And I give them respite.﴾ That is: I give them time, so that they may increase in sin. The explanation of this has passed in the surahs al-A'raf and al-Tur. The root of "mala" is a period of time from the ages; it is said: Allah gave him respite (amla Allahu lahu), meaning: He lengthened the period for him. "Mala" (with the short vowel, maqsur) is the wide earth, named for its extension. ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm.﴾ That is: strong and severe, so nothing escapes Me. He, glory be to Him, called His kindness a plan (kayd), just as He called it istidraj, because it takes the form of a plan with regard to its outcome. He described it as firm (matin) for the strength of its effect in causing destruction.

﴿Or do you ask them for a reward?﴾ He, glory be to Him, returned the speech to what preceded in His saying: ﴿Or do they have associates?﴾ That is: Or do you seek from them a reward for what you call them to, of belief in Allah? ﴿Then they are burdened with a debt.﴾ Al-maghram means the penalty (gharamah), that is: they are burdened by the penalty of that reward, and "muthqalun" means: its carrying is heavy upon them because of their stinginess in spending wealth, so they turned away from answering you for this reason. The interrogation is for rebuke and reproach against them. The meaning is: you did not ask them that, and you did not seek it from them.

﴿Or is the unseen with them, so they write?﴾ That is: the Preserved Tablet, or everything that is hidden from them. So from that unseen they write what they want of proofs which they claim indicate their saying, and they dispute with you using what they write about that, and they judge for themselves what they want, and by that they dispense with answering you and complying with what you say.

﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord.﴾ That is: for His decree, which He has decreed in His foreknowledge. It has been said: the judgment here is His giving them respite and delaying the victory of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over them. It has been said: it is what He has decreed for him of conveying the message. It has been said: this is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword.

﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾ meaning Yunus, peace be upon him: do not be like him in anger, impatience, and haste. The adverbial clause in His saying ﴿when he called out﴾ is in the accusative governed by an implied genitive (mudaf mahdhuf), meaning: do not let your condition be like his condition at the time of his calling out. The clause ﴿while he was suppressed﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial qualifier from the doer of "nadā" (called out). Al-makzum means: filled with rage and distress.

Qatadah said: Indeed Allah consoles His Prophet ﷺ, and commands him to be patient and not to hurry as the companion of the fish hurried. The story of this has already been explained in the surahs al-Anbiya', Yunus, and al-Saffat. His calling out was with His saying: ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I was among the wrongdoers.﴾ (al-Anbiya': 87). It has also been said: al-makzum is one seized by his kazm, which is the passage of breath. This was said by al-Mubarrad. It has also been said: it is the one who is restrained. The first is preferable. From it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

"And you, from love of Mayy, conceal a sorrow, afflicted in heart, wounded in the heart, suppressed."
